3jRtNUf9T6.one_liner: Adds pairwise confidence comparisons between answer-supporting paths to voting logits via a KL-regularized closed-form adjustment.
3jRtNUf9T6.problem: Sampling-based test-time scaling aggregates by answer frequency or path confidence without explicitly comparing competing answers.
3jRtNUf9T6.method: Pairwise-Guided Logit Adjustment (PGLA) combines pairwise confidence comparisons between paths supporting different answers with voting support through a KL-regularized objective, which is equivalent to an adjustment of the voting logits.
3jRtNUf9T6.key_idea: Rank answers by voting logits plus a closed-form term from pairwise path-confidence comparisons, so comparative advantage can offset weak vote counts.
3jRtNUf9T6.evidence: 10 benchmarks across mathematical reasoning, knowledge reasoning, and code generation with 7 models from 1.7B to 32B parameters, plus external reward scores and online sampling.
3jRtNUf9T6.claimed_gains: The abstract gives no numbers; a review cites Qwen3-8B gains of 4.61%, 1.78%, and 2.63% on competition benchmarks.
3jRtNUf9T6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, training-free, and well motivated by voting failure cases, with validation across diverse models, benchmarks, and aggregation baselines and an elegant closed-form logit adjustment.
3jRtNUf9T6.main_concern: Gains are small relative to variance (the competition sets have 30 problems each, with no paired significance tests), and the Condorcet framing is questioned since the score reduces to a rank-based one-versus-rest mean.

ADFQP64zux.one_liner: Contrastively aligns electron-ionization mass-spectrum embeddings with pretrained molecular-structure embeddings to predict odor from spectra alone.
ADFQP64zux.problem: Existing olfactory prediction models need the explicit chemical structure of an unknown substance at inference time, which is not directly observed.
ADFQP64zux.method: SCENT is a multi-modal contrastive learning framework that aligns EI-MS representations with pretrained chemical structure embeddings, so only mass spectra are needed at inference, and it focuses on single-compound odorants. Reviewers describe the components as an EIMS2Vec-style spectrum encoder, a Transformer encoder, a CLIP/InfoNCE loss, and frozen MolFormer/OpenPOM embeddings.
ADFQP64zux.key_idea: Distill structure-derived embeddings into a mass-spectrum encoder using a CLIP-style InfoNCE contrastive loss, so structure is needed only at training time.
ADFQP64zux.evidence: Multi-label odor descriptor prediction, a prospective perceptual panel of structurally or perceptually distinct odorants, prediction of continuous human perceptual ratings, and generalization to independently acquired laboratory spectra.
ADFQP64zux.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree olfaction is an important, underexplored problem and that predicting odor from a fast spectral measurement with structure needed only at training is a useful, clearly described framing with complementary evaluations.
ADFQP64zux.main_concern: The contribution is mainly application and evaluation with off-the-shelf components, and a spectral library-search plus structure-model baseline and fuller metrics such as AUPRC are missing.

61HXPpMUbe.one_liner: DRAFT-Solver pairs soft latent-token global attention with fine attention over a learned fixed-budget subset of mesh nodes.
61HXPpMUbe.problem: Steady-state PDE surrogates on large unstructured meshes need global interactions but extra computation only in localized, task-dependent regions, which dense attention cannot afford and prior-based sparse methods prescribe by hand.
61HXPpMUbe.method: A dual-scale architecture combines global exchange through softly constructed latent tokens with fine-grained self-attention over a learned, fixed-budget node subset. Token routing and node selection are trained end-to-end without predefined regions or masks.
61HXPpMUbe.key_idea: Select a fixed budget of mesh nodes through learned importance scores for fine attention while soft latent tokens handle global exchange, trained end-to-end.
61HXPpMUbe.evidence: Benchmarks spanning 2D and 3D aerodynamics, semiconductor-device simulation and biomolecular electrostatics, against graph-, neural-operator- and transformer-based baselines.
61HXPpMUbe.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims only competitive or improved performance relative to the baselines.
61HXPpMUbe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and the data-driven node allocation informative, with encouraging results across several physical domains.
61HXPpMUbe.main_concern: Component contributions and efficiency are not established: ablations such as coarse-only or random selection are missing and no runtime, memory or parameter counts are reported.

aoFh9Q6Toi.one_liner: Replaces per-layer norm weights with one shared vector and depth-conditioned scalers and rotations, making the emergent depth encoding explicit.
aoFh9Q6Toi.problem: Hidden-state norms grow by orders of magnitude with depth, the so-called curse of depth, which is nearly universally treated as a pathology to suppress.
aoFh9Q6Toi.method: Across 16 pretrained LLMs the paper finds that normalization weights shift in magnitude and direction with depth, jointly encoding the layer index. LayerRoPE replaces all layerwise norm weights with a single shared vector and depth-conditioned scalers that combine magnitude scaling with RoPE-style rotations.
aoFh9Q6Toi.key_idea: Parametrize each block's residual-stream gain by layer index, with depth-dependent magnitude scaling and RoPE-style rotation of one shared norm weight vector.
aoFh9Q6Toi.evidence: Analysis of 16 pretrained LLMs from 9 families, and a model ladder trained up to 100B+ tokens compared with Pre-, Post-, Peri-Norm and Layer-Norm Scaling, plus looped models, ViTs and depths up to 512 layers.
aoFh9Q6Toi.claimed_gains: Reaches Pre-Norm's 1.3B loss with 3.4x less compute, improves near monotonically up to 512 layers, and improves learning-rate sensitivity by 3-10x at under 0.02% extra FLOPs.
aoFh9Q6Toi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the experiments extensive across scales, depths and architectures with consistent improvements, and the method simple with almost no added compute and useful learning-rate stability gains.
aoFh9Q6Toi.main_concern: The necessity of rotary depth encoding is unproven, since magnitude-only scaling gives most of the gain and simpler baselines such as learnable residual gates are missing, and reading norm weights as a depth encoding is not fully justified.

BspLB4V0W5.one_liner: Characterizes generalization of l2-regularized ERM in finite-width quadratic networks, mapping scaling regimes in samples, width and regularization.
BspLB4V0W5.problem: Theoretical scaling laws mostly describe generalization against data or compute in fixed-feature or infinite-width regimes with online SGD, not jointly against trainable parameters and samples in a feature-learning model.
BspLB4V0W5.method: The paper analyzes l2-regularized empirical loss minimization for a quadratic two-layer network with structured data in a finite-sample setting, giving an explicit generalization error as a function of samples, width and regularization. Reviewers note it extends an AMP and state-evolution framework and rests on a replica-symmetric conjecture.
BspLB4V0W5.key_idea: Derive generalization error from the spectral structure (signal spikes and noise bulk) of a rank-constrained estimator, producing a phase diagram of scaling regimes as width varies.
BspLB4V0W5.evidence: Theory with an explicit error characterization, a phase diagram with data-dependent power laws and onset of interpolation, and numerical agreement checks, with reviewers noting reliance on Conjecture 1.
BspLB4V0W5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the quantitative description of how width, sample size, regularization and target spectrum interact informative, including non-monotonic error and regimes where extra width gives no leading-order benefit.
BspLB4V0W5.main_concern: The main results depend on Conjecture 1 (the replica-symmetric characterization and state-evolution extension), whose validity is not established across regimes, and the extension over prior quadratic-network analyses is limited.

h7jjGRtosD.one_liner: Open-source red-teaming framework that specifies and enforces attacker access, feedback, model, and budget so attack success rates are comparable.
h7jjGRtosD.problem: AI red-teaming evaluations use differing threat models, so attack success rates are hard to compare or reproduce; changing the attacker model and access scope alone moves ASR from 2.7% to 67.0%.
h7jjGRtosD.method: SuperRed makes attackers, targets, and benchmarks interchangeable modules under a common execution model that explicitly specifies and enforces attacker capabilities (access, feedback, model, budget).
h7jjGRtosD.key_idea: Enforce explicit attacker capabilities at runtime within a common execution model so any compatible attacker, target, and benchmark can be combined.
h7jjGRtosD.evidence: Compatible combinations of 11 attack strategies, 6 benchmarks, 13 attacker models, and 11 access scopes on chatbot and agent targets, using about USD 130,000 of inference.
h7jjGRtosD.claimed_gains: Observing target trajectories together with judge feedback raises AgentDojo ASR from 15.2% to 58.9%, and attacker budget shows diminishing returns after USD 0.19 per jailbreak task and USD 0.25 to USD 0.57 per agent task.
h7jjGRtosD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified framework addresses a real reproducibility problem in red-teaming and that the experimental effort is substantial and comprehensive.
h7jjGRtosD.main_concern: The contribution is mainly infrastructural with largely expected findings, and results lack error bars and human validation of the judge.

GoHB13XU9B.one_liner: Studies CoMM as a vision-language learner and adds an explicit image-text alignment loss within its fused space (CoMM-VL).
GoHB13XU9B.problem: Alignment-based vision-language pretraining such as CLIP is sensitive to imperfect image-text correspondence and can overlook complementary information, while CoMM lags CLIP on cross-modal tasks at larger scale.
GoHB13XU9B.method: They systematically assess CoMM, which models unique, redundant and synergistic modality interactions, across alignment quality and pretraining scale, then introduce CoMM-VL, which adds an explicit image-text alignment loss in the same fused representation space.
GoHB13XU9B.key_idea: Combine CoMM's multimodal interaction objective with an explicit image-text alignment loss on the same fused representation space.
GoHB13XU9B.evidence: Controlled comparisons with fixed data, architecture and optimizer and a fixed 3M pair count across alignment-quality subsets, evaluated on zero-shot classification, retrieval, multimodal probing and frozen-LLM transfer with CC12M and LAION-COCO pretraining.
GoHB13XU9B.claimed_gains: The visible abstract gives no numbers; a review reports that on CC12M CoMM-VL raises CoMM's ImageNet zero-shot accuracy from 33.6% to 41.8% and mean image-to-text retrieval from 33.7% to 50.1%.
GoHB13XU9B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled comparison under varying pair alignment and the substantial gains of CoMM-VL over CoMM across classification, retrieval and probing.
GoHB13XU9B.main_concern: Misalignment robustness of CoMM-VL is not directly tested (the split experiments evaluate CoMM only), and CoMM-VL changes several things at once so gains cannot be cleanly attributed.

86VXDqoDW7.one_liner: Jointly fine-tunes a CLIP text encoder with a motion diffusion model under motion and text consistency constraints for text-to-motion.
86VXDqoDW7.problem: Text encoders pretrained on proxy objectives miss subtle dynamic nuances, giving inadequate text representations for motion generation.
86VXDqoDW7.method: LeGO adapts a pretrained CLIP text encoder into LeGO-CLIP by optimizing it jointly with a motion diffusion model, so the encoder receives differentiable feedback from generation quality through a motion consistency constraint and a text consistency constraint.
86VXDqoDW7.key_idea: Backpropagate motion-diffusion generation feedback into the text encoder, regularized by motion and text semantic consistency constraints, so the encoder becomes generation-oriented.
86VXDqoDW7.evidence: Experiments on HumanML3D, KIT-ML and SnapMoGen, convergence-speed comparisons, transfer of LeGO-CLIP to other motion generators, physical keyword-control tests, and ablations.
86VXDqoDW7.claimed_gains: Claims top results on HumanML3D, KIT-ML and SnapMoGen and up to 8x fewer training iterations to converge; no metric values appear in the visible abstract.
86VXDqoDW7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is sound (CLIP is insensitive to fine-grained motion words) and that experiments across three datasets and several generators show consistent gains.
86VXDqoDW7.main_concern: Possible evaluation coupling, since the pretrained projectors use contrastive losses similar to the T2M evaluators, and the learned encoder's own contribution is not isolated in the physical control tests.

BCNnwWBAuq.one_liner: GMNO is a mesh neural operator with element-feature embeddings, pretrained across 14 industrial electromagnetism datasets in the new MaxwellBench.
BCNnwWBAuq.problem: Neural operators are mostly studied on simplified PDE data, which does not reflect the structural complexity of industrial simulations or test generalization across scenarios governed by the same PDEs.
BCNnwWBAuq.method: MaxwellBench provides 14 datasets from distinct electromagnetism applications, and GMNO uses embedding architectures for complex multi-modal PDE data on meshes, trained with a heterogeneous parallel training paradigm for large-scale training on industrial datasets.
BCNnwWBAuq.key_idea: Embed mesh-defined multi-modal inputs (element features, material curves, interface conditions) in a shared operator and pretrain it across many industrial datasets.
BCNnwWBAuq.evidence: Experiments on MaxwellBench with parameter-matched baselines, three seeds, architecture ablations, a similarly sized pretrained Transolver and few-shot adaptation to related tasks; the abstract is truncated.
BCNnwWBAuq.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before the results.
BCNnwWBAuq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value MaxwellBench as an industrially relevant benchmark that keeps mesh structure and physical inputs, and see GMNO giving promising accuracy with effective pretraining and few-shot adaptation.
BCNnwWBAuq.main_concern: Baseline fairness and generalization claims: Transolver, LNO and GAOT receive only 2D inputs while GMNO also gets 1D boundary and interface information, so the architecture's contribution is unclear.

vhGIb7G58i.one_liner: Three diagnostic checks show privileged-teacher token scores in on-policy self-distillation do not track task value.
vhGIb7G58i.problem: On-policy self-distillation treats the teacher's likelihood shift under privileged information as a token-level action value, although it measures how a prediction changes with enriched context rather than how outcome changes with a token.
vhGIb7G58i.method: The authors examine the gap along three dimensions: whether the token score tracks task success, whether feedback from the same rollout makes the score reflect agreement with its own description (and whether other-rollout feedback helps), and what behavior the training objective reinforces.
vhGIb7G58i.key_idea: Test token credit by trajectory-level AUC against correctness, by swapping same-rollout for other-rollout feedback, and by inspecting which high-entropy tokens dominate the training signal.
vhGIb7G58i.evidence: gpt-oss-20b on AIME 2025 with five token-score training configurations compared against outcome-only GRPO; a reviewer notes one seed per configuration.
vhGIb7G58i.claimed_gains: Negative result: the two-sided score separates correct from incorrect trajectories at about chance (AUC=0.505), five token-score configurations reach only 24.2--33.9% Avg@4 versus 64.2% for outcome-only GRPO, and the highest-entropy token decile carries 57--71% of total absolute signal.
vhGIb7G58i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper questions a widely used assumption and that its failure cases and three-part analytical framework are practically useful.
vhGIb7G58i.main_concern: Evidence comes from one model, one dataset (AIME 2025), and one seed, and trajectory-level AUC does not directly establish token-level credit failure.

xltMh7HhY3.one_liner: Separate positive and negative text conditions combined with opposite-sign attention responses restore adjustable CFG in few-step diffusion models.
xltMh7HhY3.problem: Few-step diffusion distillation reduces sampling cost but weakens adjustable classifier-free guidance and runtime negative prompting.
xltMh7HhY3.method: PP-CFG keeps positive and negative text conditions separate inside a shared visual backbone and combines their attention responses with opposite signs. A Scale-Time Polarity Mixer refines each condition using the guidance scale and denoising timestep, and the student keeps a continuous scale input and selectable negative prompts at one backbone pass per step.
xltMh7HhY3.key_idea: Subtract negative-condition attention responses from positive ones within one backbone pass, with a scale- and timestep-conditioned mixer varying prompt influence over denoising.
xltMh7HhY3.evidence: Wan2.1 video generation with DMD, Qwen-Image with LCM and DMD, and the NegElement-1K benchmark of 1,000 matched image and video prompt cases.
xltMh7HhY3.claimed_gains: Reaches 81.46 VBench in four steps, lower video teacher-student distances across guidance scales than step-distilled DMD, and higher target-removal rates than the corresponding teachers on NegElement-1K.
xltMh7HhY3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that losing adjustable guidance and negative prompting in few-step models is an important problem and the one-pass design works across architectures, modalities, and distillation objectives.
xltMh7HhY3.main_concern: Evaluation does not isolate the polarity mechanism or compare against dedicated fast-generator negative-prompt methods (NASA, NAG, VSF, PCM), and NegElement-1K uses template prompts with a single VLM judge.

kFVp0WM84b.one_liner: Bootstrap-free GFlowNet subtrajectory objective over turn-level intents, plus replay, prevents hierarchy collapse in multi-turn LLM reasoning.
kFVp0WM84b.problem: Optimizing only final-reward RL in multi-turn reasoning collapses the intended hierarchy and drives diverse reasoning toward short, repetitive patterns.
kFVp0WM84b.method: I-Flow structures each reasoning turn around a turn-level intent and applies GFlowNet optimization to the resulting intent hierarchy with a bootstrap-free subtrajectory objective that propagates terminal supervision across intent sequences. Successful intent structures are replayed during training.
kFVp0WM84b.key_idea: Propagate the terminal reward across intent sequences with bootstrap-free subtrajectory flow constraints so diverse high-reward intent hierarchies keep probability mass.
kFVp0WM84b.evidence: Mathematical reasoning and code generation, with ablations, a second backbone, and math-to-code structure transfer per reviews, compared against ReMA.
kFVp0WM84b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the hierarchy-collapse and reasoning-simplification failure modes are clearly identified and the flow-based method gives consistent improvements across benchmarks with supporting ablations and theory.
kFVp0WM84b.main_concern: The method relies on six predefined intent categories and takes about 54% longer per training step than ReMA, so generality and equal-compute gains are unclear.

Hz98o3dgEc.one_liner: Flow matching toward normal graphs with bounded, adaptive detector-gradient refinement generates hard pseudo-anomalies for one-class graph anomaly detection.
Hz98o3dgEc.problem: Generated negatives for graph-level anomaly detection can be too dissimilar from normal graphs or become too easy as the detector improves.
Hz98o3dgEc.method: BNFlow learns flow-matching transport toward normal graph representations and refines intermediate samples with detector feedback to make them harder negatives, bounded within each trajectory with strength adapting to the detector's discrimination ability. Continued flow matching regularizes the generator toward the normal reference during joint learning.
Hz98o3dgEc.key_idea: Truncate a noise-to-normal flow and nudge intermediate samples along bounded discriminator gradients so pseudo-anomalies stay near-normal and keep challenging the detector.
Hz98o3dgEc.evidence: Eight graph benchmarks with ablations on discriminator guidance and continued flow matching, plus theoretical analysis of the local effect of guidance and bounds on deviation from normal references.
Hz98o3dgEc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that controlling pseudo-anomaly difficulty through normal-reference transport plus bounded discriminator guidance is coherent, with the highest mean AUROC on all eight datasets and supportive ablations.
Hz98o3dgEc.main_concern: The contribution beyond existing guided generation and pseudo-anomaly methods is not clearly shown (SDM and MoEGAD are not compared), model-selection details are unspecified, and standard deviations differ across tables.

iXLKs7T3YG.one_liner: Distillation that keeps the label gradient and projects the conditional gradient so teacher matching never lowers the correct-class margin.
iXLKs7T3YG.problem: Closer imitation of a teacher does not necessarily give a better student, because a student may already discriminate the correct class more sharply than its teacher, so further KL minimization gives that discrimination back.
iXLKs7T3YG.method: The authors prove an exact condition under which full teacher-to-student KL minimization is blocked while the teacher's relative probabilities among incorrect classes remain learnable, and derive the minimum correct-class log-odds increase that compensates. TPKD keeps the label gradient intact and minimally corrects the conditional gradient so its update preserves the label step's gains against every incorrect class.
iXLKs7T3YG.key_idea: Learn only the teacher's conditional distribution over incorrect classes, projecting the update so correct-class margins against every alternative are preserved.
iXLKs7T3YG.evidence: Theorems giving a necessary and sufficient blocking condition and the minimum price of transfer, plus experiments on two datasets (CIFAR-100 and CLINC150 per reviews) with three-seed results.
iXLKs7T3YG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory is rigorous and insightful and that imitation conflicting with acquired student discrimination is a well-motivated and common problem.
iXLKs7T3YG.main_concern: Ablations show most of the accuracy gain survives without the projection, suggesting it comes from conditional-only learning, and baselines such as a tuned DKD or CE-plus-conditional-KL are missing or untuned.

KCMR4XvFWM.one_liner: Explicit two-hidden-layer constructions with special activations reach arbitrary accuracy using the minimum d+1 hidden neurons and optimal bits.
KCMR4XvFWM.problem: The exact minimum number of hidden neurons and the encoding (bit) complexity for arbitrary-accuracy uniform approximation of continuous functions on the unit cube had not been settled.
KCMR4XvFWM.method: For d at least 2 the authors construct two fixed explicit activations and closed-form networks with hidden widths d and 1, and prove d+1 is the exact minimum for locally integrable activations with affine outputs. They also give a floor-plus-exponential activation construction (widths d, 1, 2, or d, 1, 1 with a skip connection) and bit-complexity bounds for Holder classes.
KCMR4XvFWM.key_idea: Encode function values into a single scalar through a digit-extraction-style activation so a width-d then width-1 network approximates arbitrarily well, using differences along a spanning tree for optimal bits.
KCMR4XvFWM.evidence: Theory only: proofs of the exact neuron minimum and bit-complexity bounds for bounded alpha-Holder classes matching the metric-entropy lower bound.
KCMR4XvFWM.claimed_gains: d+1 is the exact minimum number of hidden neurons; for bounded alpha-Holder classes two constructions need O(eps^(-d/alpha) log(1/eps)) bits and the spanning-tree network needs Theta(eps^(-d/alpha)) bits.
KCMR4XvFWM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers who accept the results describe them as sharp, correct, and explicit, with closed-form constructions and a quantitative bit-complexity analysis.
KCMR4XvFWM.main_concern: Novelty against prior optimal-neuron and approximation results is questioned (one reviewer says the solution is already known), and the discontinuous, high-precision activations are impractical and untrainable.

FJ1uEPMYoW.one_liner: Models concepts as mean-covariance regions in embedding space and composes scenes by scaled Minkowski sum to bind attributes to objects.
FJ1uEPMYoW.problem: Concepts in foundation-model representations are usually modeled as one-dimensional linear directions or sparse features, which do not capture intra-concept variance or explain how attributes bind to specific objects.
FJ1uEPMYoW.method: Each concept (Concept-Blob) has a compact effective support parametrized by a mean vector and a covariance matrix that induces a Mahalanobis metric, and scene composition is modeled as a scaled Minkowski sum of individual blobs, including a relational and blob.
FJ1uEPMYoW.key_idea: Represent each concept as a mean-covariance blob and compose multi-concept scenes by a scaled Minkowski sum, with a relational and blob absorbing residual inter-concept interaction.
FJ1uEPMYoW.evidence: A controlled multi-concept CLEVR setting across CLIP, DINOv3, AIMv2, and SigLIP2 for images and CLIP, SigLIP2, Qwen3-Embedding, and Sentence-T5 for text, plus unCLIP qualitative decompositions.
FJ1uEPMYoW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the region-based geometric view of concepts is an interesting, clearly explained alternative to linear-direction models, with examples that support the perspective.
FJ1uEPMYoW.main_concern: Evidence is mostly synthetic (CLEVR) and the recovered components, including the claim that the relational and blob captures relations, are not directly validated.

9GLEGppCdz.one_liner: Unsupervised mesh movement enforcing global geometric equidistribution with learned vectorized indicators and Tutte-equilibrium spring coordination.
9GLEGppCdz.problem: Under limited unsupervised constraints, local density equidistribution yields physically inconsistent movements and poorly coordinated over-allocation, while supervised mesh movement needs costly theoretical supervision.
9GLEGppCdz.method: GEMove enforces global geometric equidistribution in a unified mapped space to derive vectorized movement indicators for each mesh element, and models the mesh topology as a spring system so that Tutte equilibrium coordinates movement globally.
9GLEGppCdz.key_idea: Derive per-element vectorized movement indicators from global geometric equidistribution and couple vertices through a Tutte-equilibrium spring system for global coordination.
9GLEGppCdz.evidence: Four PDE families with zero-shot generalization to unseen equations and domain geometries, real-world ocean systems, and generalization across the global Earth system covering 54 regions and 16 variables.
9GLEGppCdz.claimed_gains: Average error reduction of 24.62% across four PDE families, with zero-shot generalization to unseen equations and domain geometries and coverage of 54 regions and 16 variables.
9GLEGppCdz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unsupervised framework coherently combines a learnable anisotropic metric with Tutte-equilibrium global coordination and generalizes well empirically.
9GLEGppCdz.main_concern: The contribution of the learned anisotropic metric is not isolated by ablations, for example against a scalar density times identity, and the accuracy-cost trade-off against classical MA baselines is not established.

lHBkoPg6K4.one_liner: Analyzes repetition collapse in diffusion-LM time-series forecasting through cumulative attention gain and reduces it with SVD truncation and history-sparsified guidance.
lHBkoPg6K4.problem: Diffusion language models used for time-series forecasting can lose temporal variation and converge to pathological numerical repetitions, and the mechanism behind this is poorly understood.
lHBkoPg6K4.method: The authors identify a recurring attention geometry (shared anchor stripes, shifted-diagonal predecessor feedback, residual structure) and formalize it in a reduced dynamical model where positive cumulative anchor-background gain across depth drives anchor concentration. They test it with two training-free interventions: attention-level spectral SVD truncation and history-sparsified classifier-free guidance.
lHBkoPg6K4.key_idea: Positive cumulative anchor-background attention gain across depth concentrates attention on anchors and homogenizes positions, which SVD truncation and history-sparsified guidance reduce.
lHBkoPg6K4.evidence: Attention analysis across diffusion steps and Transformer depth in diffusion language models (LLaDA and Dream per reviews), a reduced dynamical model, and the two interventions measured on repetition and NMAE.
lHBkoPg6K4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper presents a clean empirical phenomenon with a coherent mathematical model of the attention dynamics, and that the interventions reduce measured repetition.
lHBkoPg6K4.main_concern: The practical significance and theory-to-intervention link are thin: repetition is not clearly harmful in forecasting, NMAE barely improves (and worsens on Dream), and gain reductions are small relative to the repetition drop.

MwKov10iEz.one_liner: ShutterMuse is an MLLM trained on ShutterData with SFT and RL for composition decisions, crop refinement, and pose recommendation.
MwKov10iEz.problem: Computational photography focuses on post-capture optimization, while capture-time assistance must decide whether to keep, refine, or reject a view and guide how a subject poses.
MwKov10iEz.method: The paper introduces ShutterBench (photographer-side composition decisions and spatial refinement; subject-side scene-conditioned pose recommendation) and ShutterData (130K samples with rationales and structured supervision). ShutterMuse is a unified MLLM trained with supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning, using task-specific reward models with GRPO per reviews.
MwKov10iEz.key_idea: Train one MLLM with SFT plus GRPO on task-specific rewards to output keep/refine/reject decisions, crop boxes, and pose keypoints.
MwKov10iEz.evidence: ShutterBench evaluation of general-purpose MLLMs and specialized cropping models, with a 130K-sample ShutterData training set curated with experts in the loop.
MwKov10iEz.claimed_gains: ShutterMuse achieves the strongest overall photographer-side performance on ShutterBench and competitive subject-side performance, with no numeric gains stated in the abstract.
MwKov10iEz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark and dataset are useful, the problem is practically significant, and ShutterMuse shows strong empirical performance with comprehensive evaluation.
MwKov10iEz.main_concern: The task is close to cropping and quality assessment: guidance is limited to keep/refine/reject with a crop box and 2D poses, omitting camera movement or viewpoint advice, so the capture-time claim is weakly validated.

PMq14jTY5H.one_liner: Polynomial-time reductions in both directions between robust POMDPs with polytopic uncertainty and partially observable stochastic games under omega-regular objectives.
PMq14jTY5H.problem: Robust POMDPs with unknown transition probabilities lacked a reduction that transfers complexity results for general omega-regular objectives such as reachability, safety, and LTL.
PMq14jTY5H.method: For (s,a)-rectangular RPOMDPs with polytopic uncertainty sets, the paper reduces solving under omega-regular objectives to solving POSGs, and builds a reduction in the reverse direction, establishing semantic equivalence. This yields upper and lower complexity bounds for different objectives, with corollary results for robust MDPs.
PMq14jTY5H.key_idea: Reduce robust POMDPs with polytopic uncertainty to zero-sum partially observable stochastic games, and construct the reverse reduction to show the two models are semantically equivalent.
PMq14jTY5H.evidence: Theoretical only: constructions and proofs of the reductions and complexity bounds (reviewers describe a 47-page proof); no experiments are stated.
PMq14jTY5H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the two-way reductions and the resulting complexity results are non-trivial and novel.
PMq14jTY5H.main_concern: The reduction depends on non-standard factored-prescription policies for the min player, which puts the lower-bound proof and the claimed equivalence with standard POSGs in question.

tNNCBiSaC9.one_liner: Benchmark of 17 staged streams that expand an agent's tools, skills, and specialist agents to test retention and adaptation.
tNNCBiSaC9.problem: Existing agent evaluations assume a fixed harness or place non-stationarity in the task stream, so the effect of an evolving harness of tools, skills, and agents is unmeasured.
tNNCBiSaC9.method: The benchmark builds 17 multi-stage harness streams deterministically from verifier-based benchmarks (802 tasks, 520 tools, 42 skills, 62 agents). It evaluates deployment, which measures retained competence as the harness expands, and self-evolving adaptation, which tests whether accumulated experience stays useful as new capabilities appear.
tNNCBiSaC9.key_idea: Place non-stationarity in the externally supplied harness rather than the task stream, releasing capabilities in stages so interference from an expanding catalog can be measured with a fixed model.
tNNCBiSaC9.evidence: Experiments on frontier agents across the tool, skill, and agent axes in deployment and self-evolving adaptation settings, with old-cohort reevaluation.
tNNCBiSaC9.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports qualitative findings only (harness expansion alone can degrade performance on previously solved tasks, and gains from self-evolving adaptation are inconsistent).
tNNCBiSaC9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing harness evolution as a distinct evaluation problem and identifying harness-induced forgetting are valuable, and that the deterministic stream construction is a useful contribution.
tNNCBiSaC9.main_concern: Capability annotations and the skill-evolution protocol are weakly validated (keyword-matched skill labels, unclear skill access, low skill use), and only additive expansion under one frequency ordering is studied.

owSKndTbot.one_liner: Matching tensor-wise effective learning rate, the ratio of learning rate to parameter norm, collapses LM pretraining loss trajectories across runs.
owSKndTbot.problem: It is unclear how learning rate and parameter norm jointly shape loss dynamics in language model pretraining, for example under weight decay and norm control.
owSKndTbot.method: The paper matches tensor-wise ELRs across runs with different learning rates and parameter norms and measures how closely loss trajectories collapse across optimizers, architectures, datasets, and scales. It then uses ELR to transfer a fitted functional scaling law across norm-control methods and to design an ELR schedule.
owSKndTbot.key_idea: Learning rate and parameter norm act on loss dynamics mainly through their ratio, so runs with matched tensor-wise ELR schedules follow the same loss trajectory.
owSKndTbot.evidence: Dense, MoE, and linear-attention models up to 1B parameters, several datasets, and AdamW, Muon, and Signum, with ablations on normalization design and LR-norm modulation timescale, and interventions against weight decay and Hyperball.
owSKndTbot.claimed_gains: Mean collapse errors are typically a few times 10^-3, below the seed-to-seed variation measured in a representative configuration.
owSKndTbot.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the empirical evidence convincing and broad across optimizers, architectures, and scales, and regard ELR collapse as an insightful view of training dynamics.
owSKndTbot.main_concern: Novelty is insufficiently positioned against earlier work on ELR trajectory matching and scale invariance (for example D'Angelo et al. 2024), including the explanation of delayed acceleration.

5DaGkXBgC8.one_liner: Benchmark that isolates and scores coding agents' requirement clarification and planning before any code is written.
5DaGkXBgC8.problem: Existing coding benchmarks entangle the pre-implementation phase with code execution and overlook requirement clarification, so the effects of models and harnesses on planning are unattributed.
5DaGkXBgC8.method: SWE-Plan has 392 repository-level tasks with 929 withheld critical decisions and 4,937 atomic planning obligations, and scores whether agents recover the decisions through clarification and produce complete, repository-consistent plans. Agents run in the native Plan Mode of real harnesses, with metrics checked against human judgment and downstream execution.
5DaGkXBgC8.key_idea: Withhold critical decisions from each task and score the agent separately on recovering them through questions and on covering atomic planning obligations in its plan.
5DaGkXBgC8.evidence: 8 models under 3 mainstream harnesses, with metric reliability validated by human judgment and downstream execution.
5DaGkXBgC8.claimed_gains: Clarification and planning correlate at r = 0.62 within a system; planning rankings correlate at rho = 0.63 across harnesses; a 5.5 pp change in ask rate accompanies only a 0.8 pp change in question precision.
5DaGkXBgC8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark targets a timely, genuine gap by measuring clarification and planning directly, with a principled requirements-engineering basis and realistic harness-native evaluation.
5DaGkXBgC8.main_concern: Realism and headroom are limited: a simple fixed-answer user simulator, single-plan evaluation, and checklists that may reward over-specific or copyable plan content.

VE3BBfjTFa.one_liner: A causal-inference framework and checklist for identifying validity threats in proxy, observational, and single-run foundation model research.
VE3BBfjTFa.problem: Controlled experiments at foundation-model scale are prohibitively expensive, so cheaper research strategies rely on implicit assumptions that often receive insufficient attention.
VE3BBfjTFa.method: The paper shows that proxy experiments and scaling laws, observational studies of public models, and single-run designs each estimate a treatment effect conditional on a training recipe by substituting cheaper parts of the ideal experiment. Using concepts from the empirical social sciences, it builds a unified framework with a validity profile for each strategy, illustrated with case studies of recent papers, and a checklist.
VE3BBfjTFa.key_idea: Treat each cost-saving research strategy as causal inference with substituted components, then assess it against internal, external, construct, and statistical validity and assumptions such as confounding and interference.
VE3BBfjTFa.evidence: Conceptual analysis illustrated by case studies of recent foundation model papers; no empirical benchmark is stated.
VE3BBfjTFa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the causal framing is clear and well motivated, the examples tie each validity threat to real papers, and the checklist is useful to practitioners.
VE3BBfjTFa.main_concern: The interference discussion is the least clear part, and the assumptions needed to avoid each threat are scattered across subsections rather than stated uniformly.

TCUMPNTlIq.one_liner: Mechanistically analyzes how LLMs handle negation, finding answer suppression plus candidate promotion, and trains against weak suppression.
TCUMPNTlIq.problem: LLMs often repeat the same answer under negation, and the internal mechanism behind this failure is not understood.
TCUMPNTlIq.method: A negation benchmark and mechanistic analysis identify attention heads and MLP neurons that suppress the original answer and promote a candidate; a training objective then addresses the weakness.
TCUMPNTlIq.key_idea: Negation is implemented by suppressing the original answer and promoting a favored candidate, so failures arise when suppression is weak or answer bias blocks alternatives.
TCUMPNTlIq.evidence: Open and closed-source LLMs on a negation benchmark; mechanism analysis mainly on Gemma 3-12B-IT with partial replication; training evaluated on out-of-domain benchmarks.
TCUMPNTlIq.claimed_gains: Models repeat the same answer under negation in 37-71% of cases; the abstract's reported gains for the training objective are cut off.
TCUMPNTlIq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is significant, the benchmark is broad, and the mechanism analysis is clearly linked to the failure diagnosis and training method.
TCUMPNTlIq.main_concern: Scope is narrow: mechanism analysis centers on Gemma 3-12B-IT, training uses one model and PopQA, and the benchmark covers a thin slice of negation forms.

12Dqbq8GCa.one_liner: Uses a frozen pretrained VLM to score sub-trajectory clips and prioritize them in the replay buffer for off-policy RL.
12Dqbq8GCa.problem: The replay buffer, a core RL component, is unexplored for VLM guidance, and TD-error prioritization struggles with sparse-reward tasks with delayed credit assignment.
12Dqbq8GCa.method: A frozen, pre-trained VLM acts as an automated evaluator that scores promising sub-trajectories, asynchronously and once per clip, and the semantic score is combined with TD-error-based prioritized replay. It needs no VLM fine-tuning and no change to the loss.
12Dqbq8GCa.key_idea: Score stored sub-trajectory clips with a frozen VLM that judges whether goal satisfaction is visible, then upweight those clips in replay sampling.
12Dqbq8GCa.evidence: Game-playing and robotics tasks, discrete and continuous, across four off-policy algorithms with ablations, compared mainly against uniform replay and PER.
12Dqbq8GCa.claimed_gains: Agents achieve 15-57% higher average success rates and improve sample efficiency by 35-55% compared to previous approaches.
12Dqbq8GCa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, practical, and pluggable into any off-policy algorithm, with consistent gains across algorithms that grow with task difficulty.
12Dqbq8GCa.main_concern: Comparisons omit stronger baselines such as VLM-based reward shaping and hindsight replay, and the score acts like a success detector so gains may partly come from the prioritization schedule.

k8OS5wstOa.one_liner: Audio-video world model driven by a canonical relative 6-DoF camera trajectory, trained progressively and distilled to few-step causal generation.
k8OS5wstOa.problem: Existing world models use source-specific action spaces or focus on visual prediction, making it hard to combine heterogeneous interaction and audiovisual supervision.
k8OS5wstOa.method: EchoWM canonicalizes interaction as a dataset-calibrated relative 6-DoF camera trajectory and trains an audiovisual prior, trajectory conditioning and their joint realization progressively on different data mixtures. It then converts to causal few-step deployment through audiovisual teacher forcing, self-generated distribution matching and long-horizon rollouts.
k8OS5wstOa.key_idea: Use a dataset-calibrated relative 6-DoF camera trajectory as a shared control interface across first- and third-person data, with prior, control and joint stages trained on different data mixtures.
k8OS5wstOa.evidence: WBench Navigation and SANA-WM-Bench, including long-horizon rollouts of the four-step causal variant.
k8OS5wstOa.claimed_gains: Achieves leading interactive and visual-quality performance on WBench Navigation and SANA-WM-Bench, and the four-step causal variant largely preserves these capabilities over long-horizon rollout; no numbers stated.
k8OS5wstOa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the full-stack recipe (data, unified camera control, progressive training, distillation) that brings audio-video generation into interactive world models.
k8OS5wstOa.main_concern: The contribution is largely engineering that combines existing methods, audio (especially spatial audio) evaluation is thin, and the 'omnimodal' framing is called an overstatement.

cquYBuEmV5.one_liner: Black-box coarse-to-fine typographic attack on VLM image quality assessment, jointly optimizing adversarial text and placement.
cquYBuEmV5.problem: Existing typographic attacks use generic adversarial text and heuristic placement, ignoring task-related factors and local image degradation, which limits attack effectiveness and visual plausibility on VLM-based IQA.
cquYBuEmV5.method: Q-Hack's coarse stage generates candidate texts from three IQA-related attack factors and places them using scene semantics, local degradation and depth. Its fine stage uses target-model feedback to distill effective semantic patterns and refine text content and placement.
cquYBuEmV5.key_idea: Place IQA-specific adversarial text in degraded, semantically suitable regions, then refine text and position using the target model's feedback.
cquYBuEmV5.evidence: Comparison with seven state-of-the-art baselines on three widely used IQA datasets.
cquYBuEmV5.claimed_gains: Clear advantages over seven baselines in attack effectiveness, perceptual fidelity and scene consistency; no numbers stated.
cquYBuEmV5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the IQA-specific framing and the finding that text type and placement in degraded regions affect attack strength.
cquYBuEmV5.main_concern: Perceptual fidelity and scene consistency are judged by an auxiliary VLM without a human study, and novelty is limited since joint text-placement and black-box feedback optimization exist.

TJnyOYoMdQ.one_liner: Soft-label training pools nearby inputs' responses, with radius adapted to an entropy-based subjectivity coefficient, for LLM social simulation.
TJnyOYoMdQ.problem: Accuracy-based evaluation and hard-label training treat one observed human response as truth, though human behavior is subjective and an observed response is one draw from a response distribution.
TJnyOYoMdQ.method: Introduces an entropy-based subjectivity coefficient to analyze how accuracy-based evaluation and hard-label training fail as subjectivity grows. SALT pools observed outputs from semantically nearby inputs into soft distributional labels, with an aggregation radius adapted to each input's estimated subjectivity.
TJnyOYoMdQ.key_idea: Build soft distribution labels by aggregating responses of semantically nearby inputs, with the neighborhood radius adapted to each input's estimated subjectivity.
TJnyOYoMdQ.evidence: Analysis of failures as subjectivity grows and experiments on constructed datasets (described in the appendix per reviews); the abstract is cut off.
TJnyOYoMdQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem relevant and important and the subjectivity-adaptive neighborhood approach principled and interesting.
TJnyOYoMdQ.main_concern: The statistical analysis assumes independent hard-label sampling from latent distributions while the experimental data construction differs, and dataset construction details and related work are missing from the main text.

NYmZTQDxnc.one_liner: Trains open-web video research agents with synthetic tasks, a fast local video-search simulator, and retrieval-randomized GRPO.
NYmZTQDxnc.problem: Live video interaction is too slow and unreliable for agent training, while a fixed local simulator induces retrieval shortcuts that fail to transfer to the open web.
NYmZTQDxnc.method: Three parts: a pipeline synthesizing multi-hop tasks from timestamped visual evidence with text-only shortcut filtering; a field-aligned local video simulator; and RDR-GRPO, which randomizes candidate rankings, distractors, metadata and result structure during training.
NYmZTQDxnc.key_idea: Randomize the simulator's retrieval domain (rankings, distractors, metadata, result structure) during GRPO so the policy does not overfit to simulated retrieval behavior.
NYmZTQDxnc.evidence: Video-BrowseComp with a Qwen3.5-4B agent, compared with SFT, fixed-retrieval GRPO (63 tasks) and Gemini-3-Flash-Preview, plus simulator speed and token-usage measurements.
NYmZTQDxnc.claimed_gains: 40.48% accuracy on Video-BrowseComp, comparable to Gemini-3-Flash-Preview, with 74.9% lower cumulative API-token consumption (comparison target truncated in the abstract); simulator speeds up video search by 34.5-64.6x.
NYmZTQDxnc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the simulator-plus-synthetic-task framework is a useful, practical contribution that keeps deployment-facing search and watch interfaces, and that gains over the base model are substantial.
NYmZTQDxnc.main_concern: The contribution of retrieval randomization is not isolated: the comparison with ordinary GRPO uses only 63 tasks and stops at step 70, and the margin over SFT is thin without seed variance.

MeX9roZY1l.one_liner: Training-free token selection where a frozen 3D foundation model picks consistent tokens whose key-value features anchor later video blocks.
MeX9roZY1l.problem: Autoregressive video diffusion drifts geometrically over minute-long rollouts because each block is committed once and errors accumulate.
MeX9roZY1l.method: During early denoising of each block, a frozen recurrent 3D model keeps the tokens it judges consistent with the scene so far; the generator re-encodes them at the matching noise level and injects their key-value features into the next block as soft geometric anchors. The authors also introduce SceneLongBench (100 scenes, 60-second videos).
MeX9roZY1l.key_idea: A frozen 3D model decides only which tokens to keep; those tokens are re-noised and appended as key-value context to the next block at the same denoising stage.
MeX9roZY1l.evidence: Comparison with Causal Forcing on Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B using SceneLongBench, 3D consistency metrics (TTT3R-guided selection, VGGT-based evaluation) and VBench.
MeX9roZY1l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree drift in long autoregressive video generation is a real problem and that the training-free, adapter-free token-selection design is practical, with relevant 3D metrics and ablations.
MeX9roZY1l.main_concern: Generality and genuine 3D consistency are weakly supported: only one generator is used, and geometric evaluation relies on learned reconstruction models that may share biases with the selector.

sYoemfah66.one_liner: Characterizes off-policy learning of capacity-constrained allocations without overlap and proposes a minimax-regret allocation rule.
sYoemfah66.problem: Learning capacity-constrained allocations from logged rewards is hard when the logger gives zero probability to available actions, so standard overlap and minimum-eigenvalue assumptions fail.
sYoemfah66.method: Under a shared linear reward model, a source-radius modulus captures which unresolved reward directions matter given the capacity constraints. The authors derive the exact infinite-data identification threshold for a fixed source law and a minimax-regret allocation rule (MRA) with high-probability worst-batch guarantees.
sYoemfah66.key_idea: Capacity constraints determine which unresolved reward directions matter (the source-radius modulus), so a minimax-regret rule over the consistent model set needs no overlap or minimum-eigenvalue condition.
sYoemfah66.evidence: Theory (identification threshold, marginal versus integral sample-complexity separation), simulations, and a semi-synthetic study on real LLM query contexts with small batches.
sYoemfah66.claimed_gains: A constructed family needs Theta(log(1/delta)) samples for marginal outputs but Theta(rho^-1 log(1/delta)) for integral outputs; MRA shows lower empirical failure and regret than regression and robust baselines (no further numbers).
sYoemfah66.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory is significant: guarantees without overlap or minimum-eigenvalue assumptions and a clear marginal-versus-integral sample-complexity gap.
sYoemfah66.main_concern: Computational scalability and experimental scale are unclear: the best-response step needs a bilinear or MIP solve, and experiments use tiny batches (5 units, 120 assignments) with synthetic Bernoulli rewards.

0V3HdO4HiY.one_liner: Differentially private LLM fine-tuning inside input- and output-side subspaces learned from public-data update statistics.
0V3HdO4HiY.problem: DP noise in high-dimensional update spaces degrades utility, and the low-dimensional spaces used to limit it are predefined and may not match task-relevant update directions.
0V3HdO4HiY.method: BASE learns input-side and output-side bases from public auxiliary data by capturing the principal variation of model updates, motivated by a gradient-energy preservation objective under a Kronecker-structured approximation. Private DP-SGD then trains only a small core matrix, W = W0 + P_out S P_in^T, inside that subspace.
0V3HdO4HiY.key_idea: Build input- and output-side projection bases from public-data update statistics and train only a small core matrix between them with DP-SGD.
0V3HdO4HiY.evidence: Experiments across several models, privacy budgets and benchmark tasks (including IFEval), against DP-SFT, DP-LoRA, DP-Adapter and DP-BiTFiT, with a default 10% public and 90% private split.
0V3HdO4HiY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using public data to find useful update directions before private training is sensible, the privacy argument is easy to verify, and the efficiency gain over DP-SFT is notable.
0V3HdO4HiY.main_concern: Novelty is limited relative to fixed low-rank-basis and public-data-subspace methods, and the comparisons (different DP dimensions, random public split with no distribution shift) leave fairness and robustness unclear.

BoKNgD7p47.one_liner: Jailbreaks diffusion vision-language models by optimizing image perturbations against global denoising-trajectory probabilities instead of fixed response prefixes.
BoKNgD7p47.problem: Prefix-anchoring jailbreaks (Fixed Prefix Optimization) that work on autoregressive models often fail on diffusion VLMs because of progressive refusal during denoising, and the attack surface this refinement process exposes is unexamined.
BoKNgD7p47.method: Global Probability Optimization (GPO) manipulates the global generative dynamics along the denoising trajectory of masked diffusion models rather than anchoring a prefix, and GPO-V applies it to the visual modality to produce image perturbations. Per reviews, this uses gradient-based adversarial optimization under a perturbation bound.
BoKNgD7p47.key_idea: Optimize image perturbations against the probability of the whole denoising trajectory rather than a fixed response prefix, exploiting progressive refusal in masked diffusion.
BoKNgD7p47.evidence: Empirical attack results with cross-model transferability on diffusion VLMs; reviews mention latent-space and pixel-space attacks and transfer success rates in Table 3.
BoKNgD7p47.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says GPO-V produces stealthy perturbations with exceptional cross-model transferability, without numbers).
BoKNgD7p47.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find dVLM security a timely, underexplored problem and the distinction between Immediate and Progressive Refusal a valuable insight, with a jailbreak that needs only image modification.
BoKNgD7p47.main_concern: The methodological contribution may be incremental (gradient-based adversarial optimization on images), differences from DSN and PAD are unclear, and the FPO baseline is artificially built by fixing the prefix probability at 100%.

d3YrgvL4SK.one_liner: Distills an offline RL policy into a freshly initialized student with randomly frozen units to restore plasticity before online fine-tuning.
d3YrgvL4SK.problem: Existing offline-to-online RL methods focus on value calibration and treat the offline-trained policy as a given initialization, although prolonged offline optimization progressively reduces network plasticity even after performance saturates.
d3YrgvL4SK.method: REFIT (REstoring plasticity via Fresh Initialization and policy Transfer) distills the offline policy into a freshly initialized student while temporarily freezing a random subset of student units, before online fine-tuning, to transfer offline behavior into a more plastic initialization.
d3YrgvL4SK.key_idea: Reset the policy by distilling the offline policy into a fresh student with a random subset of units frozen, giving a more plastic starting point for online learning.
d3YrgvL4SK.evidence: Controlled experiments linking prolonged offline training to lower plasticity and weaker online gains, plus D4RL and OGBench experiments on Cal-QL and IQL backbones against O2O plug-in methods (OPT and PARS per reviews).
d3YrgvL4SK.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says REFIT consistently achieves higher aggregate performance than existing O2O plug-in methods across Cal-QL and IQL backbones, with no numbers in the text provided).
d3YrgvL4SK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the plasticity reframing is clear and supported by controlled experiments showing similar offline performance can lead to different online improvement, with thorough ablations and broad environment coverage.
d3YrgvL4SK.main_concern: The practical advantage over simply stopping offline training earlier is unclear (shorter offline training performs comparably in Figure 8), and the choice of this distillation method over other plasticity methods is not justified.

vfQKqcFKbe.one_liner: Cross-modal on-policy distillation that gates each token's teacher supervision by counterfactual modality attribution and weights tokens by downstream reasoning influence.
vfQKqcFKbe.problem: Existing cross-modal on-policy distillation treats token-level supervision uniformly, conflating transferable reasoning with sensor information from a privilege modality such as depth or video that an RGB-only student cannot learn.
vfQKqcFKbe.method: LAMP uses counterfactual modality attribution to identify whether each token's teacher advantage is grounded in the student or the privilege modality, feeding a self-calibrating gate that suppresses untransferable supervision. Horizon-conditioned divergence weighting then emphasizes tokens with greater downstream influence on the reasoning trajectory.
vfQKqcFKbe.key_idea: Remove or perturb the privileged modality to test whether a token's teacher advantage survives, gate out supervision that depends on it, and upweight tokens that influence later reasoning.
vfQKqcFKbe.evidence: Depth-to-RGB and video-to-RGB transfer experiments against standard OPD and cross-modal distillation baselines; reviews mention six benchmarks, two student sizes, and self-distillation.
vfQKqcFKbe.claimed_gains: Up to 6.1% and 10.7% performance gain over the strongest baselines on depth and video benchmarks, respectively.
vfQKqcFKbe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between teacher supervision backed by student-accessible information and supervision relying on unavailable information is meaningful and well posed, with consistently positive results across benchmarks and student sizes.
vfQKqcFKbe.main_concern: Many gains are about one point or less from single runs without variance estimates, and the learnability claim and the gating mechanism are not directly validated.

aeArdjq8c7.one_liner: Learns graph coarsening for maximum independent set with a Partition GNN scoring contractions and a Representative GNN picking cluster states.
aeArdjq8c7.problem: Exact MIS solvers become slow on large graphs, hand-crafted heuristics trade away guarantees, and directly predicting independent sets with learning makes global coordination difficult.
aeArdjq8c7.method: A Partition GNN scores candidate contractions during multilevel graph coarsening and a Representative GNN selects top-k local independent-set states for each final cluster, while combinatorial search is retained for the final decision.
aeArdjq8c7.key_idea: Use learning only to guide multilevel coarsening and cluster-state selection, shrinking the graph so combinatorial search makes the final decision.
aeArdjq8c7.evidence: Erdos-Renyi graphs with up to 2,000 vertices, including 500-vertex instances with certified optima and larger 1,000- and 2,000-vertex graphs.
aeArdjq8c7.claimed_gains: On 500-vertex instances with certified optima, the average independent-set size is 19.20, or 99.5% of the optimal 19.30, and mean wall-clock time falls from 643.57 seconds for exact solving to 3.41 seconds, an approximately 189x speedup.
aeArdjq8c7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like using GNNs to shrink the search space for a combinatorial method and note good results against a strong heuristic (ReduMIS) on larger graphs.
aeArdjq8c7.main_concern: Evaluation uses only synthetic random graphs, with no real-world graphs or harder families such as near-regular expanders, and omits recent baselines and benchmarks such as OnlineMIS and RB graphs.

YIgT41au2t.one_liner: Closed-form propagation of 3D Morphable Model parameter variance to per-vertex variance via the law of total variance.
YIgT41au2t.problem: Mapping 3DMM parameter-space variance to per-vertex variance by sampling or error propagation is computationally expensive.
YIgT41au2t.method: CLUE (Closed-form Local Uncertainty Estimation) applies the law of total variance to the 3DMM formulation to obtain a closed-form per-vertex approximation, exploiting linear blend skinning and the kinematic hierarchy per reviews. It is integrated into in-the-wild human mesh recovery training and inference and released as SAM 3D Body (CLUE) with high-resolution uncertainty maps.
YIgT41au2t.key_idea: Apply the law of total variance to the skinned 3DMM, splitting pose and shape/expression variance along the kinematic chain, to get per-vertex variance without sampling or Jacobians.
YIgT41au2t.evidence: Qualitative and quantitative experiments on joint, mesh, and uncertainty metrics with Spearman uncertainty-to-error correlation; reviews mention three 3DMMs, 3DPW, and seven datasets that use SAM 3D Body predictions as pseudo-ground truth.
YIgT41au2t.claimed_gains: When used in training, CLUE outperforms probabilistic and deterministic baselines on joint, mesh, and uncertainty metrics and has the highest uncertainty-to-error Spearman correlation; reviews cite FLAME runtime of 3.4 ms versus 226.4 ms for Jacobian-based propagation and memory of 4.3 MB versus 410.4 MB.
YIgT41au2t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the closed-form derivation is clear and mathematically motivated and gives large speed and memory savings over sampling or Jacobian-based propagation.
YIgT41au2t.main_concern: Approximation quality is not quantified (it assumes independent parameters with diagonal covariance and first-order rotation uncertainty), and calibration is validated mainly with visual maps and pseudo-ground truth from another model.

EB3UnwGdtD.one_liner: Chunk-wise autoregressive driving video diffusion that stores generated object appearances and retrieves them by geometry-grounded attention at object locations.
EB3UnwGdtD.problem: Objects in driving world models can reappear with altered appearance after disappearing even when motion and geometry are correct, because the model reproduces where objects are but not what they looked like.
EB3UnwGdtD.method: ReDreamer uses persistent object identities and geometry in scene controls as addresses for appearance memory, recording generated appearances and retrieving them at current object locations through geometry-grounded attention. To fix exposure bias from training with real references but reading generated appearances at inference, it uses rollouts that build and read their own memory, supervised by distribution matching distillation.
EB3UnwGdtD.key_idea: Use object identities and projected geometry as addresses into an appearance memory of the model's own generated frames, trained with self-rollouts and distribution matching distillation.
EB3UnwGdtD.evidence: A nuScenes-derived re-entry evaluation with a Re-entry Appearance Consistency (RAC) score and a front-view FVD comparison with MagicDrive-V2; reviews note a Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B base model and 320x480 resolution.
EB3UnwGdtD.claimed_gains: Improves RAC by 10.5% over the strongest evaluated baseline, enabling memory reads improves RAC by 12.0%, and with four denoising steps per chunk FVD falls 5.7% relative to MagicDrive-V2 while generating at 8.1 FPS.
EB3UnwGdtD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the re-entry failure mode clearly defined and the geometry-grounded, instance-bound memory a well-motivated, efficient design that addresses exposure bias.
EB3UnwGdtD.main_concern: Scope and evaluation are limited: the memory depends on supplied instance IDs and 3D boxes, covers only vehicles, and neither the RAC metric at 320x480 nor the Wan2.1 base-model advantage is isolated.

z0aI9NAAd1.one_liner: Learns an image-level color cast state representation and conditions an sRGB white-balance correction network on it.
z0aI9NAAd1.problem: Nonlinear ISP processing entangles intrinsic scene colors with color casts, so sRGB white-balance correction cannot tell which chromatic variations to remove, especially when large regions of intrinsic scene color resemble a cast.
z0aI9NAAd1.method: The color cast state (CCS) explicitly characterizes the tendency and severity of color casts, and a structured CCS is learned from paired incorrectly white-balanced and ground-truth images using tendency and severity supervision with soft similarity learning. The learned CCS then conditions the correction network, which removes casts while preserving intrinsic scene colors.
z0aI9NAAd1.key_idea: Learn a continuous, supervised color-cast embedding (tendency and severity with soft similarity) and feed it as an explicit condition to the correction network.
z0aI9NAAd1.evidence: Experiments on public benchmark datasets (the abstract is cut off before specifics); reviews note test sets rendered from RAW with the same preset white-balance settings used for training and casts in a 2850K-7500K range.
z0aI9NAAd1.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text provided claims leading results on public benchmarks but cuts off before any numbers).
z0aI9NAAd1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the color-cast ambiguity clearly motivated and the separation of CCS learning from correction simple and coherent, directly targeting a gap in prior sRGB white-balance methods.
z0aI9NAAd1.main_concern: Novelty is moderate because the components (LoRA-adapted ViT, soft contrastive learning, FiLM conditioning, Restormer-style backbone) are established, and testing covers only global uniform casts rendered the same way as training.

5jHBQU6HQl.one_liner: Training-free hierarchical token compression for long-document QA across encoder output, prefill page budgets, and layer-adaptive KV-cache selection during decoding.
5jHBQU6HQl.problem: Long-document QA is expensive because of long visual-token sequences, and compressing the context without disrupting document structure or losing cross-page evidence is hard.
5jHBQU6HQl.method: After visual encoding, Bottom-up Background Token Merging reduces background redundancy while preserving layout cues. During prefilling, Adaptive Page-level Token Assignment converts question-conditioned attention into soft page budgets and selects tokens within each page, and during generation layer-adaptive dynamic KV-cache compression reselects active visual context across decoder depths at each step.
5jHBQU6HQl.key_idea: Compress visual tokens in three stages: merge background tokens, allocate soft per-page budgets from question attention, and reselect active KV entries per layer at each decoding step.
5jHBQU6HQl.evidence: Four document QA benchmarks; reviews mention DUDE, MP-DocVQA, MMLongBench, a Qwen3-VL-8B extension, and a token-matched comparison against global token selection.
5jHBQU6HQl.claimed_gains: Reduces the final active visual-token budget to under 20% of the original input while preserving 94.94-98.72% of baseline performance and achieving 1.50x-4.05x LLM-stage speedups.
5jHBQU6HQl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree page-to-token allocation is supported by a token-matched control against global selection, and the evaluation covers meaningful long-document workloads with official test splits and a larger backbone.
5jHBQU6HQl.main_concern: Dynamic KV-cache selection is under-specified (storage of inactive KV, per-layer application, head aggregation), and matched final token ratios do not mean matched compute budgets.

AXreM7ZFsz.one_liner: Advances a world-action model's predictive future as a recurrent state across control rounds, with adaptive refresh from a confidence module.
AXreM7ZFsz.problem: World-action models repeatedly compute predictive futures for control at substantial inference cost, and asynchronous execution limits effective action-generation throughput through the overhead of temporal correction.
AXreM7ZFsz.method: The Further-Future Propagator (FFP) treats the predictive state as a recurrent state and learns a future-to-further-future transition that advances it across control rounds, shaped by action relevance and a recurrent manipulation context. The composed state conditions the frozen native action pathway, and a Confidence module estimates the value of a fresh native WAM prediction to trigger adaptive refresh instead of a fixed schedule.
AXreM7ZFsz.key_idea: Learn a future-to-further-future transition reused as a recurrent input across control rounds, refreshing from the WAM only when estimated marginal value is high.
AXreM7ZFsz.evidence: Three architecturally distinct world-action models (hidden state, future-video latent, and fused K/V pairs) per reviews, with real-robot evaluation on four tasks and per-module latency measurements.
AXreM7ZFsz.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text provided cuts off at 'Across three architecturally' before any numbers).
AXreM7ZFsz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find framing predictive futures as updatable recurrent states a practical alternative to fixed refresh schedules, with generality shown across three distinct world-action models, real-robot tests, and supportive ablations.
AXreM7ZFsz.main_concern: Headline gains are measured against asynchronous baselines that lose quality, so the method ends roughly level with synchronous execution rather than ahead of it, and part of the throughput gain may come from counting conventions.

pgcODLzF8Q.one_liner: Reduces each brain MRI view to a few 2D PCA-and-detail components before frozen 2D foundation-model encoding and linear probing.
pgcODLzF8Q.problem: Using pretrained 2D foundation models on volumetric brain sMRI requires bridging the mismatch between a 2D encoder and a 3D volume, and existing methods encode slices independently and integrate their features afterwards.
pgcODLzF8Q.method: Multiscale Volumetric Reduction (MVR) compresses each anatomical view from D slices into M much smaller than D complementary 2D components: an uncentered-PCA base component from through-plane intensities plus residual detail components from multiscale spatial descriptors. The reduction is estimated from training volumes without labels or gradient-based optimization, components pass independently through a shared frozen 2D foundation model, and features are concatenated for linear probing.
pgcODLzF8Q.key_idea: Reduce the volume before encoding using a label-free PCA base component plus multiscale residual detail components, rather than encoding slices independently and fusing features afterwards.
pgcODLzF8Q.evidence: ADNI, OASIS, and ABIDE under a frozen-encoder setting against 2D-to-3D adaptation and input-reduction baselines, with ADNI-to-AIBL external validation and ablations.
pgcODLzF8Q.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports strong overall performance on ADNI, OASIS, and ABIDE and strong ADNI-to-AIBL generalization without numbers).
pgcODLzF8Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea simple and practical, the paper clear and well written, and the evaluation across three datasets with external validation and ablations fair.
pgcODLzF8Q.main_concern: Uncertainty reporting is weak (only fold standard deviations with overlapping intervals, and the same AIBL test set for all models), and results are limited to three brain MRI classification datasets without released code.

RGyWnuFJEp.one_liner: Learns a goal-conditioned progress-distance field over VLA features to give dense transition-level advantages for RL fine-tuning.
RGyWnuFJEp.problem: Sparse task-level outcomes give little credit to intermediate transitions in long-horizon VLA manipulation, and existing progress-aware methods predict progress as an unstructured scalar.
RGyWnuFJEp.method: A lightweight shared Progress Field head maps current and goal representations from pretrained VLA features into a compact progress space, where geometric distance defines goal-conditioned value, shaped by temporal and goal-structure objectives. Value changes across transitions become dense progress advantages for offline advantage-weighted imitation and online RL fine-tuning.
RGyWnuFJEp.key_idea: Goal-conditioned value is the distance between current and goal embeddings in a learned progress space, and its change across a transition is the dense advantage.
RGyWnuFJEp.evidence: Experiments on LIBERO, RoboTwin2.0, and real-world bimanual manipulation; reviews note a matched comparison with a reproduced RLinf-GRPO baseline over three training seeds, ablations, and four real-world tasks against EvoRL.
RGyWnuFJEp.claimed_gains: The abstract excerpt is cut off before any numbers; reviews cite LIBERO-Long rising from 96.8% to 99.0% and RoboTwin from about 79% to 92%.
RGyWnuFJEp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit a coherent goal-conditioned value formulation and gains over the reproduced GRPO baseline under matched initialization, data, and budgets.
RGyWnuFJEp.main_concern: Gains are confounded with the progress-weighted offline initialization, the signal may reflect execution speed rather than task progress, and comparisons with SimpleVLA-RL and SRPO are missing.

4iw4bN65Cg.one_liner: Benchmark for editing CAD programs from 2D drawings plus instructions, with a joint RL method for reconstruction and editing.
4iw4bN65Cg.problem: Parametric CAD editing assumes access to source programs, but designers often start only from dimensioned 2D drawings and text instructions, and no benchmark covers this end-to-end task.
4iw4bN65Cg.method: CAD-D2E pairs dimensioned orthographic views and instructions with executable source and edited programs; JORE generates both programs in one autoregressive policy and is trained with CARPO, an RL objective motivated by giving reconstruction and editing component-specific credit.
4iw4bN65Cg.key_idea: One autoregressive policy emits the source program then the edited program, with RL credit assigned per component so reconstruction reward is not charged to editing actions.
4iw4bN65Cg.evidence: CAD-D2E covers 15 edit subtypes and five part families, with a fully human-reviewed, source-disjoint test set; reviews note broad baselines including IterCAD, controlled Direct variants, and ablations, scored by IoU, Chamfer distance, and executability.
4iw4bN65Cg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the task is practically motivated and the benchmark is carefully built, with paired executable programs, a human-reviewed source-disjoint test set, and broad baselines.
4iw4bN65Cg.main_concern: The global IoU, Chamfer distance, and executability metrics do not verify that the requested local edit was made, and CARPO is not shown to help editing specifically or beyond this benchmark.

KCWUnOvhuL.one_liner: BIRD unifies LLM-based iterative reward design methods in one benchmark, showing simple design choices beat prior methods.
KCWUnOvhuL.problem: LLM-based reward-design methods differ in implementation details, feedback assumptions, and evaluation environments, so they cannot be compared directly.
KCWUnOvhuL.method: BIRD expresses existing methods in one configuration and evaluation space under matched feedback and policy-training budgets, so individual design choices can be ablated and new components prototyped; a small set of helpful choices is then combined.
KCWUnOvhuL.key_idea: Express each iterative reward design method as a configuration of swappable design choices, ablate each under matched budgets, and combine the ones that consistently help.
KCWUnOvhuL.evidence: Experiments on MuJoCo, Meta-World, Assistax, and HumanoidBench; reviews report 6 methods on 21 tasks, 30 ablated design choices, and a small user study with author annotators.
KCWUnOvhuL.claimed_gains: No numbers are stated; the abstract says combining a few simple design choices performs significantly better than the evaluated prior methods.
KCWUnOvhuL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree BIRD is a clear, useful unified framework and that the finding that only a few of 30 design choices help consistently is valuable.
KCWUnOvhuL.main_concern: Ablations change several factors at once and do not disentangle interactions or LLM dependence, and the human study uses only author raters.

GulLUy9nKq.one_liner: Learned robotic world model with separate differentiable dynamics and vision modules, enabling gradient-based policy optimization and system identification.
GulLUy9nKq.problem: Existing world models focus on unconstrained latent or visual imagination, not physically grounded, differentiable simulation usable for control and physical inference.
GulLUy9nKq.method: OrbiSim separates explicit physical-state dynamics from visual observation generation and conditions the dynamics on structured scene assets and object attributes, so gradients flow through the simulation loop for contact modeling, sparse-reward policy optimization, and physical inference.
GulLUy9nKq.key_idea: Condition a neural dynamics model on asset and physical-parameter descriptors and keep it separate from rendering, so gradients to states and parameters pass through the whole loop.
GulLUy9nKq.evidence: The abstract reports comparisons with world models on predictive fidelity and control; reviews cite a Newton initial-velocity experiment, Cable Lift, and Push control tasks.
GulLUy9nKq.claimed_gains: The abstract claims higher predictive fidelity and control performance than existing world models without numbers; a review cites Push success of 42.71% versus 25.00%.
GulLUy9nKq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit separating explicit dynamics from visual rendering, which exposes physical parameters for optimization, and downstream evidence beyond prediction metrics.
GulLUy9nKq.main_concern: Evidence does not show contact or non-penetration is handled on unseen geometries or that the model is more efficient than conventional simulators, and the Push success criterion is inconsistent.

ntZt8q7B4v.one_liner: Signed token attribution for LLM responses by propagating masking-induced log-probability change backward via secant slopes with local conservation.
ntZt8q7B4v.problem: Explaining how context tokens support or oppose a fixed reasoning-model response needs signed, additive attributions that scale to long contexts and cover both attention and linear-attention models.
