ntZt8q7B4v.method: DeltaTrace measures the response log-probability change when explained context tokens are masked, distributes it with operator-specific finite-change rules composed backward through the graph via effective secant slopes, and assigns each token its embedding displacement times the backward slope. Auxiliary memory grows linearly with sequence length.
ntZt8q7B4v.key_idea: Replace gradients with secant slopes over the finite masking change, composed backward so token attributions sum exactly to the response log-probability difference.
ntZt8q7B4v.evidence: Deletion faithfulness (RISE, MAS) and needle-in-a-haystack recall on retrieval and reasoning tasks; reviews cite Qwen3-8B and a hybrid Qwen3.5-9B with Gated DeltaNet, compared with FlashTrace and others.
ntZt8q7B4v.claimed_gains: On the evaluated attention model it has the lowest RISE and MAS on most retrieval and reasoning tasks and the highest needle-in-a-haystack recall, exceeding FlashTrace by 5.67-24.33 percentage points.
ntZt8q7B4v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is principled, gives signed attributions that sum to the score change, and handles both attention and linear-attention models efficiently.
ntZt8q7B4v.main_concern: Results depend on a single EOS reference and masking scheme with no sensitivity tests, only two Qwen models are used, and DeepLIFT and Integrated Gradients comparisons are missing.

hVIN8o7qlY.one_liner: Co-evolves rubrics with the policy, turning each response's unmet rubric criteria into teacher contexts for on-policy self-distillation.
hVIN8o7qlY.problem: On-policy self-distillation relies on privileged teacher contexts built independently of each rollout and fixed before training, so they cannot adapt to specific errors or to the improving policy.
hVIN8o7qlY.method: MR.RLSD uses rubrics as a shared interface: rubric scores set the policy-update direction, while criteria unmet by each response become online teacher contexts that give contrastive feedback to modulate token-level update magnitudes. A shared policy acts as both response generator and teacher.
hVIN8o7qlY.key_idea: Rubric criteria a response fails are converted online into contrastive teacher contexts, so token-level self-distillation guidance is response-specific and evolves with the rubrics.
hVIN8o7qlY.evidence: Benchmarks across several domains with two models, comparisons with baselines including EvoRubric, and ablations such as random criteria selection; reviews note GPT-OSS-120B scores responses and verifies new rubrics.
hVIN8o7qlY.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract excerpt; reviews describe the gains as modest but leading on most benchmarks for both models.
hVIN8o7qlY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that response-specific teacher guidance from unmet rubrics is a sensible way to improve on-policy self-distillation and that average benchmark scores improve.
hVIN8o7qlY.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate self-distillation from evolved-rubric RL, gains are modest with no variance across training runs, and the extra cost of external judging is not reported.

rxzSY4Cw0T.one_liner: Two-stage GCD method that reweights anchor-relative residual features in cosine classification after structure-regularized adaptation.
rxzSY4Cw0T.problem: In fine-grained generalized category discovery, cosine classification scales residual directional similarity by the product of sample and prototype residual magnitudes relative to a known-class anchor, weakening subtle discriminative cues.
rxzSY4Cw0T.method: Stage one adapts pretrained representations under known-class supervision, constraining local relations with a momentum reference encoder. Stage two builds a semantic anchor per novel prototype, applies square-root reweighting to residual magnitudes, and uses a novelty-and-ambiguity gate to apply the correction selectively.
rxzSY4Cw0T.key_idea: Decompose embeddings relative to a known-class semantic anchor and square-root reweight residual magnitudes so small discriminative residuals are not suppressed in cosine scores.
rxzSY4Cw0T.evidence: Six benchmarks with comparisons to GCD methods, ablations, and hyperparameter sensitivity; reviews note a DINO-initialized ViT backbone.
rxzSY4Cw0T.claimed_gains: Average overall accuracy of 71.9% across six benchmarks; a review lists 76.4% on CUB-200 and 70.1% on Stanford Cars.
rxzSY4Cw0T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the residual-magnitude view of cosine scoring is a sensible perspective on fine-grained GCD and that evaluation on six datasets with ablations is fairly comprehensive.
rxzSY4Cw0T.main_concern: Empirical evidence for the magnitude-suppression claim is thin, the residual correction adds only about one point in ablations, only a DINO backbone is tested, and tables report inconsistent numbers.

q6v74ymt03.one_liner: Injects ground-truth cross-view correspondence supervision at output, attention, and scene-token levels of a feed-forward 3D reconstruction model.
q6v74ymt03.problem: In feed-forward multi-view reconstruction, matching supervision confined to a dedicated head shapes internal representations only indirectly, leaving cross-view interactions weakly constrained.
q6v74ymt03.method: LEVER adds a dense Match Head that predicts pixel-level cross-view displacement fields, constrains selected cross-view attention responses with patch correspondences, and has sequence-level scene tokens aggregate cross-view information under a correspondence-consistency constraint. Targets come from existing 3D ground truth, without external flow teachers.
q6v74ymt03.key_idea: Make cross-view correspondence a training signal at three levels: dense displacement output, attention weights on matched patches, and consistency of global scene tokens.
q6v74ymt03.evidence: Five benchmarks covering camera pose, depth, and 3D reconstruction, with ablations of each supervision level (run on a smaller model and reduced data per reviews).
q6v74ymt03.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the three-level supervision design is coherent and results are strong across several datasets, with separate ablations of matching, attention, and scene-token supervision.
q6v74ymt03.main_concern: Main comparisons use public checkpoints with different encoders, data, and training, and ablations use a smaller model, so gains cannot be attributed to the method itself.

I1TWEAI1RU.one_liner: Training-free image-editing acceleration that reuses velocities in non-edit regions and extrapolates them in edit regions with time-dependent weight.
I1TWEAI1RU.problem: Training-free acceleration for instruction-based editing with diffusion transformers reuses cached velocities or rescales their magnitudes at skipped timesteps, which compromises fine detail.
I1TWEAI1RU.method: REVE separates edit from non-edit regions by the agreement between predicted velocities and reference velocities that reconstruct the reference image. At skipped timesteps it reuses velocities in non-edit regions and extrapolates them in edit regions, with a weight that grows as denoising moves from structure formation to detail refinement.
I1TWEAI1RU.key_idea: Extrapolation sharpens edit regions but creates artifacts elsewhere while reuse preserves non-edit content, so apply each by region with a time-increasing extrapolation weight.
I1TWEAI1RU.evidence: Step1X-Edit, Boogu-Image-0.1-Edit, and LongCat-Image-Edit on GEdit-Bench and GIE-Bench, with equal-latency comparisons, ablations, and integration with adaptive methods per reviews.
I1TWEAI1RU.claimed_gains: 2.54-2.73x speedups, matching or exceeding the compared training-free methods.
I1TWEAI1RU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the region-dependent reuse versus extrapolation is well motivated and gives consistent quality-efficiency results across three editors and two benchmarks.
I1TWEAI1RU.main_concern: Gains over RegionE are not isolated because REVE keeps its spatial computation and KV caching, and quality validation relies on similarity to unaccelerated outputs and a single VLM judge.

28LiMirlkC.one_liner: Unified image-video encoder family trained on public data with reference-token distillation and snapshot-replay weight interpolation.
28LiMirlkC.problem: Leading vision encoders depend on non-public training corpora, so comparable encoders cannot be trained from public resources.
28LiMirlkC.method: COKE-ViT-H (0.6B) and COKE-ViT-G (1.9B) share image-video weights. Visual Reference Pretrain adds visual supervision through dedicated reference tokens, Snapshot-Replay periodically interpolates video-trained weights with a fixed image-pretrained checkpoint and resumes training, and the 1.68B-pair COKE-1.7B corpus is built with concept balancing, filtering, and deduplication.
28LiMirlkC.key_idea: Periodically interpolate video-trained weights with a fixed image-pretrained checkpoint and resume training, and distill visual-teacher features through dedicated reference tokens instead of pooled patches.
28LiMirlkC.evidence: Controlled COKE-ViT-H-256 ablations, fixed-budget data ablations, and benchmarks on classification, retrieval, video, and multimodal understanding against encoders such as SigLIP 2 and PE-G per reviews.
28LiMirlkC.claimed_gains: Snapshot-Replay improves image and video averages over continuous video-only fine-tuning by 1.81 and 1.03 points; the abstract's COKE-CLIP-G result is cut off.
28LiMirlkC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the work shows competitive encoders can be trained from public data and released-model priors, with clear, reproducible data curation, though results are comparable rather than clearly better than baselines.
28LiMirlkC.main_concern: Ablations run at reduced scale without full-scale controls, components resemble existing techniques, and benchmark leakage and hyperparameter selection on reported benchmarks are unchecked.

HlGa2G4W27.one_liner: Constant-size slot memory for long video generation, written and read by camera pose rather than time.
HlGa2G4W27.problem: Long-horizon video generation needs bounded memory that still recalls what was seen at a place after long absences, but explicit-geometry memories grow in storage and recurrent memories fade with time.
HlGa2G4W27.method: SMART keeps content in a constant-size slot recurrence whose writes are addressed by the observing camera and whose reads are queried by the rendering camera, with no explicit 3D. Each read yields a confidence estimate that conditions a chunk-causal diffusion transformer to trust retrieved content selectively.
HlGa2G4W27.key_idea: Address memory slots by camera pose through region tokens so recall depends on inter-view geometry instead of recency, with read confidence gating the generator.
HlGa2G4W27.evidence: Long trajectories in Memory Maze and Minecraft; reviews cite memory-only ablations, a same-size dense memory that collapses, slot visualizations, and baselines including a state-space recurrent memory and a ground-truth-depth geocache.
HlGa2G4W27.claimed_gains: The abstract claims high-fidelity recall far beyond the training horizon with constant memory and per-step cost, without numbers.
HlGa2G4W27.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that addressing memory by pose rather than time is a clean, well-motivated idea with strong long-horizon recall at constant cost, supported by ablations.
HlGa2G4W27.main_concern: Novelty over existing pose-addressed sparse memories is unclear, baselines are weak or lack pose inputs, and evaluation covers only simple Memory Maze and Minecraft scenes.

EDIsrhg3Fk.one_liner: Black-box agent distillation that builds preference pairs from expert and learner trajectories, labeled by realized return rather than source.
EDIsrhg3Fk.problem: Agent distillation methods either imitate expert trajectories or correct student ones, and treat teacher behavior as the target regardless of its realized quality.
EDIsrhg3Fk.method: BRIDGE forms comparisons from expert- and learner-induced histories and labels them by realized trajectory quality, so either side can be the positive. It explores recurrent states, ends local comparisons when environment states reconverge, and trains with DPO using only teacher text and environment feedback.
EDIsrhg3Fk.key_idea: Decouple trajectory source from preference direction: pick the winner of each expert-versus-learner branch by return and stop the comparison once environment states reconverge.
EDIsrhg3Fk.evidence: WebShop, ALFWorld, and ScienceWorld with two student model families; reviews cite Teacher+ and K=0 ablations and comparisons with SFT, OPD, and TCOD.
EDIsrhg3Fk.claimed_gains: The abstract excerpt is cut off before results; a review cites gains over SFT of 7.45/5.84/3.18 points in Table 1.
EDIsrhg3Fk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling trajectory provenance from preference direction is reasonable and that the Teacher+ ablation supports labeling by realized return.
EDIsrhg3Fk.main_concern: Novelty over ETO and IPR style preference methods is limited, ablations do not isolate recurrent-state selection or reconvergence truncation, and baselines such as Agentic-DPO are missing.

oh483ijJht.one_liner: Speculative decoding that jointly selects parametric and retrieval draft nodes under one budget, splicing retrieval at any parametric node.
oh483ijJht.problem: Hybrid parametric-and-retrieval drafters pick sources per round or use fixed attachment rules, missing retrieval matches that parametric draft tokens expose within a round.
oh483ijJht.method: SpecSplice treats the root and every node of a parametric draft as splice points, scores each candidate with a unified survival-probability contribution score, and builds the tree best-first using score bounds to skip retrieval queries that cannot affect selection. The paper proves the tree maximizes total score under the node budget.
oh483ijJht.key_idea: Score retrieval and parametric candidates with one survival-probability objective and expand best-first with score bounds, so retrieval is queried only at splice points that can enter the tree.
oh483ijJht.evidence: Four agentic workloads and three target models plus an optimality proof; reviews cite ablations, alternative drafters, batching, and non-agentic benchmarks.
oh483ijJht.claimed_gains: Up to 6.91x speedup over autoregressive decoding and 13-37% higher throughput than the strongest baseline on every agentic model-workload pair.
oh483ijJht.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified, prefix-aware tree objective is simple and principled and gives consistent speedups on agentic workloads without hurting non-agentic ones.
oh483ijJht.main_concern: Novelty over existing hybrid speculators is moderate, hyperparameters appear tuned on evaluation traces, and retrieval latency and overheads are not analyzed.

IiSiU1cEJI.one_liner: Builds soft-constraint preference pairs by reversing a constraint into its contrary and verifying the planted constraint can be recovered.
IiSiU1cEJI.problem: Preference data for soft constraints is labeled by LLM judges with their own biases, and a soft constraint often changes responses too little for a judge to compare.
IiSiU1cEJI.method: REVERB reverses one soft constraint to get two mirrored prompts, labels each response as preferred under its own prompt, and discards pairs where an LLM seeing only the two responses cannot recover the reversed constraint. One open-weight model runs the pipeline and yields 7,949 verified pairs for DPO.
IiSiU1cEJI.key_idea: Fix preference labels by construction through constraint reversal, and filter pairs by whether a verifier can recover the planted constraint from the responses alone.
IiSiU1cEJI.evidence: DPO on two student models evaluated on two constraint-following benchmarks against SFT, SbSM, and a judge-labeled pipeline, with human validation and general-capability checks.
IiSiU1cEJI.claimed_gains: Up to 18.4 points better constraint following on two benchmarks across two student models, beating the judge-labeled pipeline by up to 12.3 points with fewer pairs.
IiSiU1cEJI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reversal-plus-recovery design is clean, data quality control and human validation are careful, and REVERB beats baselines while keeping general capability.
IiSiU1cEJI.main_concern: Baselines are narrow, since RPO and Crab use similar ideas but are not compared, and margins over SFT and SbSM are small on some metrics without significance tests.

JOo32CtWHH.one_liner: Derivative-free diffusion guidance via value-weighted Gaussian candidates, corrected by whole-path independence Metropolis-Hastings, with error bounds independent of guidance depth.
JOo32CtWHH.problem: Reward-guided diffusion must steer sampling and correct bias from approximate value functions, but SMC with full multinomial resampling can need particle counts that grow linearly with guidance depth.
JOo32CtWHH.method: Stein Guidance selects among centered Gaussian candidates weighted by value, approximating gradient guidance in expectation with as few as two queries per step. The same queries give an explicit path weight for a whole-path independence Metropolis-Hastings correction.
JOo32CtWHH.key_idea: Value-weighted selection from centered Gaussian candidates matches gradient guidance in expectation via Stein's identity, and the same queries supply path weights for an MH correction.
JOo32CtWHH.evidence: A Brownian example against SMC and a proof of superpolynomial decay of finite-grid total variation error in the number of MH updates under uniform value and spatial regularity bounds; reviews mention experiments without detail.
JOo32CtWHH.claimed_gains: No numeric gains are stated; the abstract claims superpolynomial decay of total variation error in the number of MH updates, with constants that do not grow with guidance depth.
JOo32CtWHH.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers credit a simple, elegant derivative-free guidance method with provable convergence guarantees, while a third could not position it against existing literature.
JOo32CtWHH.main_concern: The criticism of SMC considers only multinomial resampling, runtime comparisons and an unguided MH baseline are missing, and the writing is hard to follow.

tRJJkeMtby.one_liner: Pairs a frozen linear truth probe with two-sided intervention along the same direction to measure sensitivity loss under sycophancy.
tRJJkeMtby.problem: Language models can keep decodable truth information while their answers change under user pressure, and probe accuracy alone does not show how strongly answers respond to that information.
tRJJkeMtby.method: PSI fits a linear truth direction, freezes the probe, and applies a two-sided intervention along the same direction on matched cue and neutral prompts. It adds component removal, donor-rescue and route interventions, and a validation-selected amplification test.
tRJJkeMtby.key_idea: Measure truth-direction sensitivity as the change in answer logits between positive and negative perturbation along the fitted probe direction, and compare it between cue and neutral conditions.
tRJJkeMtby.evidence: Qwen2.5 (7B, 14B, 32B) and Gemma-2 (9B, 27B) with matched cue-neutral comparisons, component removal on five models, donor-rescue and route interventions on two models, and prediction on unseen context families.
tRJJkeMtby.claimed_gains: Normalised response drops by 0.25-0.41 no-cue-response units while answer accuracy stays within a 2-percentage-point equivalence range, and PSI improves prediction of later accuracy failures by 0.07-0.10 AUROC on unseen context families.
tRJJkeMtby.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is simple and interpretable and that separating probe decodability from intervention sensitivity and answer accuracy is interesting, with sensible controls.
tRJJkeMtby.main_concern: A fixed honest-condition truth direction may rotate under pressure, the sensitivity metric measures response to external perturbation rather than the model's own use of truth, and cross-model results are incomplete.

jYLRArW7rw.one_liner: Block-wise LLM quantization objective that penalizes reconstruction errors along Fisher-curvature directions estimated from cached score vectors.
jYLRArW7rw.problem: Block-wise reconstruction for post-training quantization penalizes all block-output perturbation directions equally even though they affect the final predictive distribution differently.
jYLRArW7rw.method: SABRE approximates the Fisher curvature of the full-precision predictive distribution with rank-one outer products of sampled score vectors, adds penalties on errors aligned with those directions on top of isotropic reconstruction, and bounds token weights by gradient-norm normalization. Score vectors are computed once and cached, and only the loss changes, so it plugs into existing block-wise methods.
jYLRArW7rw.key_idea: Weight block reconstruction error by its projection onto token-wise score vectors (a rank-one Fisher approximation), normalized by gradient norm, alongside the plain isotropic loss.
jYLRArW7rw.evidence: Integration into Block-AP, OmniQuant, and FlexRound for low-bit LLM quantization per reviews; the abstract excerpt is cut off before the experiments.
jYLRArW7rw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the objective is well motivated and easy to integrate as a plug-in loss that leaves optimization variables and inference unchanged, with promising low-bit results.
jYLRArW7rw.main_concern: Novelty over gradient- and curvature-based reconstruction objectives is not demonstrated, score-caching memory and per-model strength tuning are not profiled, and evaluation scope is narrow.

30JtoWYlQT.one_liner: Benchmark scoring vision-language models on answering and abstaining as one unit across original and edited images in charts and scenes.
30JtoWYlQT.problem: Visual question answering needs correct answers when evidence suffices and abstention when it does not, but per-view answerability accuracy hides failures where both must hold for the same question.
30JtoWYlQT.method: A benchmark over PlotQA charts, CLEVR scenes, and GQA photographs groups each question with independently presented original and edited images, and success requires every supported answer and every required abstention. Chart labels are verified by executable witnesses that give different answers but identical masked pixels.
30JtoWYlQT.key_idea: Score each question as one group across evidence changes and certify missing-information chart labels with pairs of complete charts that differ in answer but share the same masked image.
30JtoWYlQT.evidence: 72,000 responses from six configurations; CLEVR adds 1,000 structural witnesses and a 100-group pixel replay, GQA is scored under original-label and permissive policies across six models, and controlled interventions probe Gemma.
30JtoWYlQT.claimed_gains: Highest complete task success is 57.0% on charts and 43.5% on CLEVR, GQA's original-label maximum is 33.7%, and permissive GQA scoring yields 51.2-63.5% across six models.
30JtoWYlQT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and the group-level metric, backed by executable chart witnesses, exposes failures hidden by per-view accuracy.
30JtoWYlQT.main_concern: Scene label validity for CLEVR and GQA is weakly verified and occlusion appearance is an uncontrolled confound, with only six open-weight models and simple edits tested.

2FJWogibpF.one_liner: Proves vanilla flow matching has constant-depth expressive power and that self-conditioning lifts it to space-bounded Turing machines.
2FJWogibpF.problem: Iterative samplers such as flow matching seem suited to visual reasoning because each step could act as a reasoning step, but extra sampling steps may not add computational depth.
2FJWogibpF.method: A circuit-complexity analysis shows that, under mild regularity conditions, the vanilla flow-matching trajectory can be simulated by a constant number of sequential rounds of parallel model evaluations. It then shows that conditioning on the previous step's estimate of the final image removes this bottleneck, and tests this on visual-reasoning tasks.
2FJWogibpF.key_idea: Self-conditioning feeds the previous step's estimate of the final image back into the model, creating sequential dependence that lets a constant-depth backbone simulate space-bounded Turing machines.
2FJWogibpF.evidence: Theorems on simulation by constant parallel rounds and Turing-machine equivalence with self-conditioning, plus controlled experiments on diverse visual-reasoning tasks with matched training compute per reviews.
2FJWogibpF.claimed_gains: No numbers are stated; the abstract says self-conditioned flow matching reaches higher accuracy and greater reasoning depth than vanilla flow matching and improves with more sampling steps.
2FJWogibpF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical perspective is clear and useful and that the empirical gains over vanilla flow matching are consistent in controlled comparisons.
2FJWogibpF.main_concern: The upper bound assumes a global, time-uniform Lipschitz bound that does not hold for the ideal flow and is only estimated empirically, so the theory may not explain finite-budget behavior.

IwGbzyFF9v.one_liner: Optimism-based RL with abstention: regret bound depends on realized interactions, plus lower bounds in effective horizon and gap.
IwGbzyFF9v.problem: Agents that may terminate an episode for a fallback reward need regret guarantees that reflect fewer interactions when abstention occurs, rather than the full decision budget HK.
IwGbzyFF9v.method: The paper formulates abstention as an augmented MDP and runs an optimism-based algorithm that includes abstention in value iteration and policy execution. The leading regret term depends on the realized number of interactions, and the optimal effective horizon d* and minimum gap gamma_min characterize when abstention helps.
IwGbzyFF9v.key_idea: Add abstention as an action with known fallback value inside optimistic value iteration, so regret scales with realized interactions and effective horizon rather than the full budget HK.
IwGbzyFF9v.evidence: Theoretical regret upper bound and complementary lower bounds, illustrated by three examples where abstention is never beneficial, uniformly optimal, or beneficial depending on parameters.
IwGbzyFF9v.claimed_gains: No numbers are stated; the abstract claims a potentially sharper upper bound when abstention reduces interactions and lower bounds showing the dependence on d* and gamma_min is unavoidable.
IwGbzyFF9v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the abstention setting is reasonable, the paper is clearly written, and the upper and lower bounds appear sound.
IwGbzyFF9v.main_concern: The setting reduces to a standard tabular MDP with an absorbing state, so UCBVI-style arguments apply and the d*-dependent improvement may not beat existing bounds such as UCBVI-BF.

tOb3TKEFBU.one_liner: Adapts a 33B video generator into an interactive world model via LoRA, language-grounded actions, and temporal attention routing.
tOb3TKEFBU.problem: Large video generators support only coarse zero-shot language control of character and camera, and precise per-latent action control usually needs dedicated action modules or heavy adaptation.
tOb3TKEFBU.method: Each action is a structured combination of character and camera instructions aligned with the corresponding temporal video latents, and temporal attention routing restricts each instruction to its intended time interval. Adaptation is a LoRA on MiniMax-H3 with no dedicated action modules.
tOb3TKEFBU.key_idea: Encode actions as time-aligned natural-language instructions and mask attention so each instruction affects only its own interval, reusing the video model's pretrained text pathway.
tOb3TKEFBU.evidence: 8,000 gameplay samples and 10,000 LoRA steps; reviews cite a comparison with a geometry-supervised baseline (SolarWM) on four control channels and an inverse-dynamics evaluation, with generation quality shown mostly qualitatively.
tOb3TKEFBU.claimed_gains: Effective character and camera control from 8,000 gameplay samples, 10,000 LoRA optimization steps, and 0.199% trainable parameters while preserving generation quality; a review says it matches or exceeds SolarWM on 3 of 4 control channels with 3.2% of its trainable parameters.
tOb3TKEFBU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the recipe is simple and cheap, reusing the language interface with a small LoRA and little data, with a sound evaluation setup.
tOb3TKEFBU.main_concern: The claims that the language prior drives control and that generation quality is preserved are not isolated or quantified, with no text-free action-token baseline and no quality metric against the frozen model.

w1UuNbUBWN.one_liner: Redistributes GRPO advantages over action chunks of failed VLA rollouts by temporal optimal-transport alignment to a successful rollout.
w1UuNbUBWN.problem: Sparse terminal feedback and costly robot interactions make VLA reinforcement learning inefficient, and learned reward models need extra data construction and training.
w1UuNbUBWN.method: GTPO pairs each failed rollout with its nearest successful in-group teacher using the policy's visual features, aligns them with temporally masked optimal transport, and produces normalized action-chunk weights that redistribute the GRPO advantage while retaining terminal rewards. Teachers evolve with the policy.
w1UuNbUBWN.key_idea: Temporally masked optimal transport between a failed rollout and its nearest successful rollout yields chunk-level weights that reallocate the uniform GRPO trajectory advantage.
w1UuNbUBWN.evidence: LIBERO (four suites), RoboTwin, and five real-world fine-manipulation tasks; reviews cite comparison with GRPO, a one-demonstration warm start, and AUC-SR and early-SR efficiency metrics.
w1UuNbUBWN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extracting credit assignment from the policy's own rollouts without a reward model is well motivated, with comprehensive simulation and real-robot experiments.
w1UuNbUBWN.main_concern: Ablations lack a shuffled-weight control that separates temporal credit from generic advantage reweighting, and the base VLA models used are unclear.

Mr11TIpz1a.one_liner: Proper scoring rules for right-censored survival data by passing the forecast through the censoring mechanism before scoring.
Mr11TIpz1a.problem: Event times in survival analysis are only partially observed under right censoring, so proper scores for probabilistic forecasts do not apply directly.
Mr11TIpz1a.method: The predictive distribution is mapped through the censoring mechanism and a proper score is applied to the induced observed-data law, giving localized scores for fixed censoring times and marginalized scores for random or partially observed censoring. This recovers censored likelihood and IPCW criteria, yields censored CRPS, pinball, Brier, and energy scores, and gives a sample-based censored engression objective for multivariate survival.
Mr11TIpz1a.key_idea: Score the censored version of the forecast rather than the forecast itself, so the censoring adjustment never depends on the forecast being scored.
Mr11TIpz1a.evidence: Proofs of propriety under conditionally independent censoring and identification of the latent joint CDF for strictly proper base scores, plus experiments where the scores rank the oracle forecast correctly across several censoring regimes.
Mr11TIpz1a.claimed_gains: not stated; a review notes some margins are very small, such as a Brier score of 0.0457 versus 0.0460.
Mr11TIpz1a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is principled and theoretically thorough, recovers existing criteria such as censored NLL and IPCW Brier as special cases, and extends to multivariate survival.
Mr11TIpz1a.main_concern: Experiments lack comparisons with established baselines in single-event and competing-risks settings and rely on a single N=1000 set without seeds or confidence intervals.

5nmkbdcMvZ.one_liner: Distills instruction-adaptive checklist reasoning into a direct four-dimension image-editing reward model via reliability-weighted on-policy self-distillation.
5nmkbdcMvZ.problem: Scalar reward prediction compresses multidimensional editing preferences, broad criteria miss instance-specific editing and preservation constraints, and long reasoning from generative evaluators is costly for online RL.
5nmkbdcMvZ.method: Each editing condition is decomposed into atomic checklist requirements with four-dimensional score labels and verification evidence. After supervised initialization, a privileged teacher sees checklists, item-level judgments, and rationales to supervise the student's own scoring trajectories, weighted by agreement with reference labels, and the deployed student predicts four score distributions directly without checklists or reasoning.
5nmkbdcMvZ.key_idea: A teacher conditioned on checklists supervises the student's own score-token trajectories, weighted by teacher-reference agreement, so the student scores directly without reasoning at inference.
5nmkbdcMvZ.evidence: Three reward benchmarks across multiple model scales, the CheckDistill-40K dataset, and downstream RL on Qwen-Image-Edit compared with UniWorld-Qwen-Image-Edit per reviews.
5nmkbdcMvZ.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract excerpt; reviews note strong results on three reward benchmarks and substantially fewer output tokens at inference.
5nmkbdcMvZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the instance-specific atomic checklists give structured supervision and the method balances accuracy with efficiency, with strong results across reward benchmarks.
5nmkbdcMvZ.main_concern: Novelty over existing on-policy self-distillation is limited and not isolated, and downstream RL baselines omit reward models trained specifically for image-editing evaluation.

DsF9dWgvpF.one_liner: Living benchmark of 43 biomedical datasets comparing classical, neural, and tabular foundation models across 28 feature-by-sample operating points.
DsF9dWgvpF.problem: Biomedical tables with thousands of variables but only tens to hundreds of labelled samples are poorly represented in general-purpose tabular benchmarks.
DsF9dWgvpF.method: 43 biomedical datasets are evaluated under a shared cross-validation protocol on a grid of 28 feature-by-sample operating points, comparing classical estimators, neural networks, tabular foundation models, and AutoGluon as a separate reference. Fold-level predictions and an interactive leaderboard are released and open to new datasets.
DsF9dWgvpF.key_idea: Evaluate every model on a controlled grid of feature counts and training sample sizes so rankings can be read per operating point and per biomedical modality.
DsF9dWgvpF.evidence: 43 datasets, 28 operating points, a paired bootstrap over the target pool for Elo comparisons, and AutoGluon's one-hour extreme preset at the reference and full cell.
DsF9dWgvpF.claimed_gains: At 10,000 features and 100 training samples RealTabPFN 2.5 has the highest point estimate, separated from TabPFN 3 by 87 Elo (95% interval [43, 129]).
DsF9dWgvpF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it fills a relevant benchmarking gap for high-dimensional, low-sample biomedical data, with a rigorous, detailed setup and a useful live leaderboard.
DsF9dWgvpF.main_concern: Dataset selection screens with Random Forest and may bias the collection, and novelty and the transfer of rankings across biomedical modalities are limited.

dpOjIHiDKY.one_liner: Joint 3D reconstruction and generation in a shared anchor-view space, with per-voxel selection of the best-supported input view.
dpOjIHiDKY.problem: Camera-relative reconstruction and canonical-space generation have a coordinate mismatch, and conditioning each 3D location on all views mixes useful geometry with unrelated image content.
dpOjIHiDKY.method: A shared anchor-guided space follows the anchor view's azimuth while keeping the canonical upright direction, and reconstruction and generation branches exchange features bidirectionally to predict per-view point maps and a sparse voxel structure. Pixel-to-voxel correspondences then select the input view with the strongest valid support for each voxel.
dpOjIHiDKY.key_idea: Define a space aligned to the anchor view's azimuth so reconstruction and generation can exchange features, then pick each voxel's best-supported view through pixel-to-voxel correspondences.
dpOjIHiDKY.evidence: Reviews cite component studies on anchor-guided joint training (Table 2), point-map error (Table 3), and view selection (Table 4), run on synthetic renderings; the abstract excerpt is cut off before the experiments.
dpOjIHiDKY.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract excerpt; a review cites sparse-structure IoU rising from 0.4563 under cross-space joint training to 0.5827 with anchor-guided training.
dpOjIHiDKY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the anchor-guided shared space addresses the coordinate mismatch coherently, with informative component studies and convincing quantitative and qualitative results.
dpOjIHiDKY.main_concern: The contribution over Mix3R and ROAR-3D is not isolated, the three-stage pipeline can propagate upstream errors, and evaluation uses synthetic renderings rather than real unposed images.

XfutYzVRFq.one_liner: Quality-blind stopping rule for agentic loops that detects settling when successive edit sketches stop moving in a common direction.
XfutYzVRFq.problem: Agentic generate-evaluate loops cannot see true output quality and usually run a fixed round budget, so they keep running after improvement has stopped.
XfutYzVRFq.method: Each artifact is hashed into a sketch whose per-round update is the round's edit, and a coherence statistic measures the share of recent update magnitude that carries the artifact a net distance. LoopStop scores each change by how far coherence lies below a closed-form settled value that depends on the decay setting, and accumulates these scores into a stopping decision.
XfutYzVRFq.key_idea: Once a loop settles, successive edits stop moving the artifact in a common direction, so low coherence of hashed update sketches relative to a derived closed-form value signals settling.
XfutYzVRFq.evidence: A proof that no quality-blind detector can tell whether quality rises or falls, a closed-form coherence value, and experiments on ARC-AGI, BigCodeBench-Hard, and MLAgentBench-Kaggle with several evaluator types per reviews.
XfutYzVRFq.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract excerpt; a review says LoopStop reaches similar accuracy at much lower cost and latency in Table 2.
XfutYzVRFq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that stopping agent loops without hidden-test access is a practically important problem and that the sketch-based statistics add low overhead across diverse evaluator types.
XfutYzVRFq.main_concern: The theory uses a mean-ratio approximation and assumes independence of overlapping statistics, evaluation reports partial-credit metrics rather than task success, and gains on some datasets are small.

fLMfgC7z2G.one_liner: Event-guided BEV updating that refreshes LiDAR detections during blind intervals using depth-lifted event features and support-gated temporal fusion.
fLMfgC7z2G.problem: LiDAR detectors run at the slowest sensor's rate, leaving 50-100 ms blind intervals without updated detections, and the RoI-based Ev-3DOD updates only individual detections.
fLMfgC7z2G.method: A frozen LiDAR reference detector is coupled with an event-driven branch that updates a sparse BEV representation through each blind interval. Frustum Event Lifting lifts event features with an inference-time LiDAR depth prior, and Support-Gated Temporal Fusion combines fresh event evidence with cached LiDAR features.
fLMfgC7z2G.key_idea: Lift event features into BEV with a LiDAR depth prior and gate their fusion with cached LiDAR features by support, instead of propagating each box with RoI motion.
fLMfgC7z2G.evidence: DSEC-3DOD and Ev-Waymo against Ev-3DOD, with component ablations and temporal analysis per reviews; uses only LiDAR and events, without RGB.
fLMfgC7z2G.claimed_gains: Outperforms Ev-3DOD in every evaluated category by up to 8.6 AP on DSEC-3DOD and 12.2 AP on Ev-Waymo.
fLMfgC7z2G.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the BEV reformulation of blind-time detection is well motivated and gives strong, consistent improvements on two benchmarks with efficient RGB-free inference.
fLMfgC7z2G.main_concern: The comparison with Ev-3DOD changes the reference detector, head, and sensors at once, so gains are not isolated to event-guided BEV updating, and FEL and SGTF build on known techniques.

al7TXa807t.one_liner: Exact worst-case error for min-aggregation graph networks computed from weights, with finite teaching sets certifying all graphs and execution lengths.
al7TXa807t.problem: It is unclear when errors on a small teaching set certify a learned graph algorithm on unseen graphs and at arbitrary execution lengths.
al7TXa807t.method: For nonnegative, bias-free min-aggregation networks of arbitrary width, the paper computes the exact worst-case relative error against Bellman-Ford from the weights alone and characterizes which fixed labeled endpoints suffice. It also derives the optimal error amplification over execution lengths, which guides readout design.
al7TXa807t.key_idea: Compute worst-case error against Bellman-Ford directly from the weights and show that finitely many fixed teaching endpoints control it, with amplification set by which channels teaching exposes.
al7TXa807t.evidence: Theorems on exact identification (two fixed labeled endpoints for K-step execution, K+2 endpoints for equality of teaching and global error) and a small experiment with ten paired fits.
al7TXa807t.claimed_gains: In ten paired fits, adding one teaching graph reduces mean global error from 32.26% to 0.0862%, with improvement in every pair.
al7TXa807t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is important and the theoretical results are detailed, sound, and strong, including exact worst-case characterization and sharp long-horizon amplification bounds.
al7TXa807t.main_concern: Guarantees hold only for a restricted class of nonnegative, bias-free min-aggregation networks, experiments are small and synthetic and do not test readout optimization, and the paper is hard to follow.

NHIvVFCBol.one_liner: Pipeline turning merged-PR discussions and revisions into verifiable code-review tasks and verifier-filtered training trajectories.
NHIvVFCBol.problem: Code review yields open-ended natural-language findings with no general test-based verifier, so scaling verified review training data is hard.
NHIvVFCBol.method: The pipeline collects merged GitHub PRs, reconstructs the code snapshots reviewers examined, and uses a curation agent to consolidate findings across discussions and revisions, labeling each supported, opposed, or uncertain and binding it to the snapshot. A finding-level verifier filters teacher trajectories by crediting supported high-priority findings and penalizing opposed ones.
NHIvVFCBol.key_idea: Treat PR history as implicit verification: findings later accepted or fixed count as supported, withdrawn or rejected ones as opposed, and a verifier scores trajectories against these labels.
NHIvVFCBol.evidence: From 556k PRs, 168k review tasks in eight languages and 60k verified trajectories; evaluated on Lego-Review-Bench with human validation of the LLM judges and ablations per reviews.
NHIvVFCBol.claimed_gains: F1 rises from 5.7 for the base model to 43.1 on Lego-Review-Bench; the abstract excerpt is cut off after that figure.
NHIvVFCBol.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using PR histories as a scalable, audited finding-level supervision signal is practical and well evaluated, with human validation of the LLM judges and clear scaling effects.
NHIvVFCBol.main_concern: PR history is a noisy proxy for correctness (about 5.1% of supported high-priority findings do not hold), the benchmark is small, and smaller differences lack uncertainty estimates.

mEE3hChoIx.one_liner: Sharp approximation rate (JT)^(-1/d) for looped ReLU networks with J stored modules and T calls, dependent on loop allocation.
mEE3hChoIx.problem: How the amount and timing of module reuse jointly determine approximation accuracy in looped networks remains largely open.
mEE3hChoIx.method: The paper studies multi-stage looped ReLU networks with J stored modules and T total calls, proving matching upper and lower bounds of order (JT)^(-1/d) with an explicit recurrent construction, then characterizes which call schedules attain that rate.
mEE3hChoIx.key_idea: Error scales with the product JT, so extra calls offset fewer modules, but only if a constant fraction of calls remains after a constant fraction of modules is visited.
mEE3hChoIx.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower bounds for bounded unit-Lipschitz functions on [0,1]^d; no experiments are stated.
mEE3hChoIx.claimed_gains: Optimal worst-case uniform error of order (JT)^(-1/d) for fixed d and every 1 <= J <= T.
mEE3hChoIx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the results give clear, matching bounds that unify known endpoints, and that the paper is readable and honest about its limits.
mEE3hChoIx.main_concern: The constructions rely on real-valued weights of unlimited precision that store large amounts of information, and novelty over prior looped-network results is questioned.

HNKBCnaShl.one_liner: Training-free activation sparsity for SiLU LLMs using lazy recentering, activation- and weight-aware rotation, and fused corrections.
HNKBCnaShl.problem: SiLU-based LLMs have little natural activation sparsity, and imposing high sparsity substantially degrades accuracy.
HNKBCnaShl.method: Lazy shift recenters SiLU activations around zero and defers the correction to the end of the FFN, while a rotation that uses both activation and weight information reduces sparsification error. The shift and rotation corrections are fused to turn the gains into decoding speedup.
HNKBCnaShl.key_idea: Recenter gated-FFN activations around zero with a precomputable deferred correction so both Up and Down projections can sparsify, and rotate using joint activation and weight statistics.
HNKBCnaShl.evidence: Five models at 50% and 60% sparsity compared with TEAL, plus decoding speed on an RTX 5090 and a second hardware platform per reviews, with ablations.
HNKBCnaShl.claimed_gains: At 50% and 60% sparsity, average accuracy over TEAL improves by 1.60 and 3.29 percentage points across five models, with up to 1.72x decoding speedup over the dense model on an RTX 5090 at 50% sparsity.
HNKBCnaShl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree lazy shift is a concrete, well-isolated improvement for gated FFNs, with consistent quality gains at high sparsity and measured decoding speedups.
HNKBCnaShl.main_concern: Comparisons with TEAL mix different calibration data and a sparse LM head, so gains are not shown under equal conditions, and some definitions are inconsistent.

N5RAVYx0b3.one_liner: ExpGYM benchmarks LLM agents under costly-feedback budgets; PoolAct coordinates feedback acquisition across parallel agents with shared observations.
N5RAVYx0b3.problem: When external feedback is costly, agent capability depends on how it acquires information as well as how it reasons, but standard evaluations ignore feedback budgets.
N5RAVYx0b3.method: ExpGYM uses pre-cached feedback and deterministic surrogates for hyperparameter tuning, multi-hop search, and evidence audit to re-evaluate agents under different budgets while preserving feedback charges. PoolAct shares observations and exploration state across agents to coordinate acquisition.
N5RAVYx0b3.key_idea: Replay costly feedback from cached deterministic surrogates while still charging for it, and let parallel agents pool observations and exploration state so requests are not duplicated.
N5RAVYx0b3.evidence: Six models under Free Feedback, Moderate Budget, and Tight Budget settings on three tasks with trajectory analyses; PoolAct with 4 agents under matched per-agent budgets and component ablations.
N5RAVYx0b3.claimed_gains: Gemini 3.8 Flash's multi-hop search AVG falls from 71.9% to 17.6% between Free Feedback and Tight Budget, and PoolAct raises Qwen3.8's Moderate Budget evidence-audit exact evidence-set accuracy from 68.8% to 93.7% with 4 agents.
N5RAVYx0b3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the cached-surrogate benchmark enables reproducible budget-constrained evaluation and that PoolAct improves evidence-audit performance, with supportive ablations.
N5RAVYx0b3.main_concern: Exact-match caching assumes deterministic, stateless tools, and PoolAct lacks cost-matched comparisons against a single agent with the same total budget or simpler partitioning baselines.

FaTXdk2WIv.one_liner: Splits hash bits into a class-center head and a residual head trained on K-means sub-clusters to keep intra-class ordering.
FaTXdk2WIv.problem: Hash-center methods push every same-class sample to one binary center, so codes encode the class but not the semantic ordering among same-class items, which class-level mAP does not measure.
FaTXdk2WIv.method: RICH splits the N bits between a center head trained on the superclass label and a residual head trained on sub-clusters found by K-means in the pretrained embedding, with the number of sub-clusters set automatically from per-class sample count and codebook capacity. The paper also proposes the Intra-class Spearman and Semantic Recall@k metrics.
FaTXdk2WIv.key_idea: Separate bit subsets for class identity and for sub-cluster residual structure avoid the interference that arises when both objectives share one bit space.
FaTXdk2WIv.evidence: A coarse-label setting that trains on superclass labels and withholds subclass labels for evaluation; reviews note multiple datasets, bit widths, backbones, and ablations at equal bit budgets with pretrained-feature and ITQ alternatives.
FaTXdk2WIv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the intra-class ordering gap in hash-center methods is a real problem and that the new metrics and subclass-level evaluation are useful, with extensive empirical evaluation.
FaTXdk2WIv.main_concern: Evaluation selects checkpoints on the query set, claims about other hashing paradigms are overly broad, and differentiation from prior multi-center and order-preserving hashing is thin.

HzIoMQjraJ.one_liner: Trains a query router and a pool of LLM agents together in one RL loop, routing by predicted familiarity scores.
HzIoMQjraJ.problem: Mixture-of-Agents routers fitted to a frozen pool cannot track later agent updates, and agents are not given competence-aware data that would induce complementary expertise.
HzIoMQjraJ.method: A predictive familiarity estimator maps intermediate hidden states to a score for how well an agent matches a query, without full rollouts or external judges. Cumulative-threshold routing activates the smallest score-ranked subset whose scores sum to a threshold, and the same scores steer training queries toward agents becoming proficient on related inputs.
HzIoMQjraJ.key_idea: Hidden-state familiarity scores both route queries, via the smallest top-ranked subset summing to a threshold, and direct training queries toward emerging specialists.
HzIoMQjraJ.evidence: Multiple domains (math reasoning, code generation, instruction following, general reasoning per reviews) with three shared-backbone configurations and a heterogeneous pool, in-distribution and OOD tests, and ablations of the estimator and exploration.
HzIoMQjraJ.claimed_gains: The abstract says the system outperforms static-agent routers and fine-tuning pipelines with a fixed collaboration workflow, without numbers.
HzIoMQjraJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly optimizing routing and agent training is meaningful and the experiments are extensive across domains and agent pools, with useful ablations.
HzIoMQjraJ.main_concern: Controls are missing to show gains come from router-agent feedback rather than extra training or data allocation, and the familiarity score is heuristic, with single-seed results and possible train-test overlap.

LZkt4JLPXT.one_liner: Semi-supervised adverse-weather restoration that keeps failed teacher predictions as contrastive negatives and adds a phase-spectrum semantic constraint.
LZkt4JLPXT.problem: Unified weather-removal models generalize poorly to real scenes because they rely on synthetic supervision and weak semantic constraints.
LZkt4JLPXT.method: A student-teacher framework stores failed teacher predictions in an unreliable database as contrastive negatives and high-quality predictions in a reliable database as positives. It adds a phase-spectrum semantic constraint in place of text-based supervision and an adaptive phase consistency loss that balances input and teacher pseudo-ground-truth by degradation severity.
LZkt4JLPXT.key_idea: Use the teacher's failed outputs as hard negatives alongside reliable pseudo-labels as positives, and constrain Fourier phase as an inexpensive semantic prior.
LZkt4JLPXT.evidence: Real-world weather-removal benchmarks, composite degradations, different backbones, efficiency comparisons, and a downstream detection experiment per reviews.
LZkt4JLPXT.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says only that it consistently outperforms existing methods on real-world benchmarks.
LZkt4JLPXT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that retaining failed teacher predictions as negatives is an intuitive idea with clear gains in component ablations across several backbones and tasks.
LZkt4JLPXT.main_concern: Unreliable samples are defined by relative NR-IQA scores, which may label acceptable restorations as failures, and the claim that Fourier phase supplies semantics is overstated.

pznSjITDAD.one_liner: Relation-aware token attention over node, mesh-edge, and contact-edge token groups for deformable solid dynamics prediction.
pznSjITDAD.problem: Contact dynamics for deformable solids need both local interactions and long-range deformation, but multi-hop message passing is costly and compressing states into a few latent tokens loses fine local detail.
pznSjITDAD.method: RATIO aggregates nodal states and two kinds of edge features, intra-body mesh relations and inter-body contact relations, into separate token groups, applies attention across the groups, and maps the result back to update node and edge states. Reviews note it can be fused with a local simulator such as MGN.
pznSjITDAD.key_idea: Tokenize nodes, mesh edges, and contact edges into separate banks and run attention across them so local relation types enter a compact global interaction.
pznSjITDAD.evidence: Reviews cite two small rigid-deformable contact benchmarks (CG and TM), baselines covering local, global, and hybrid methods at comparable parameter counts, 104-step autoregressive rollouts, and runtime measurements.
pznSjITDAD.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract excerpt; a review cites RATIO+MGN reducing positional RMSE from 4.41 to 2.51 on CG and from 8.60 to 5.45 on TM relative to MGN-T.
pznSjITDAD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that bringing contact relations into global token interaction is simple and meaningful and gives clear gains over strong local, global, and hybrid baselines.
pznSjITDAD.main_concern: The advantage over prior graph tokenization such as Unisoma is not isolated, evaluation covers only two small benchmarks, and training cost is higher than several baselines.

zyJCwpB2VR.one_liner: Early-exit reasoning compression that detects answerability and then finishes the response with a compact recurrent latent module.
zyJCwpB2VR.problem: Early-exit methods stop reasoning once an answer is extractable, but reasoning models often become answerable well before they are ready to produce a high-quality response, a Solution-Response Gap.
zyJCwpB2VR.method: SCOUT identifies when the reasoning state becomes answerable, and BRIDGE uses compact recurrent latent computation to cover the remaining consolidation before the final response is generated.
zyJCwpB2VR.key_idea: Separate answerability from response readiness: detect the first, then replace the intervening explicit reasoning with a trained recurrent latent computation.
zyJCwpB2VR.evidence: Multiple reasoning benchmarks and different reasoning-model backbones, with judge-based response quality checked by human comparisons of 150 response pairs per judge, plus ablations, sensitivity analyses, and end-to-end latency per reviews.
zyJCwpB2VR.claimed_gains: Reduces average token usage by 22.1-49.6% while outperforming competing compression methods in accuracy and quality.
zyJCwpB2VR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing answerability from response readiness is a valuable formulation and that results across models and benchmarks show efficiency gains with maintained accuracy and quality.
zyJCwpB2VR.main_concern: Ablations do not separate latent consolidation from added training on high-quality responses, response readiness is defined retrospectively, and the cost of building the supervision is unquantified.

f37Cafxt0E.one_liner: Federated local training with curvature-aware and global-direction-consistency constraints, adaptively weighted per mini-batch, for globally flatter solutions.
f37Cafxt0E.problem: Locally flat solutions from sharpness-aware local training can become inconsistent after aggregation under heterogeneous client data, so local flatness does not give global flatness.
f37Cafxt0E.method: FedCADC uses a curvature-aware constraint to suppress local updates toward perturbation-sensitive regions and a direction-consistency constraint to align local trajectories with the global optimization trend, with weights adapted to each mini-batch's optimization geometry.
f37Cafxt0E.key_idea: Penalize local updates toward perturbation-sensitive regions and align local update directions with the global trend, each weighted by mini-batch optimization geometry.
f37Cafxt0E.evidence: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 (ResNet-20 per reviews) against recent federated and flatness-driven methods, plus analysis of optimization, generalization, and flatness discrepancy.
f37Cafxt0E.claimed_gains: Higher accuracy in most heterogeneous settings and generally flatter global solutions than recent methods, without numbers; a review notes it wins 12/18 settings.
f37Cafxt0E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the gap between local and global flatness is a meaningful problem and that the adaptive two-constraint design comes with optimization and generalization analysis.
f37Cafxt0E.main_concern: The curvature-aware term resembles an adaptively weighted SAM, adaptive weighting does not consistently beat fixed coefficients, results are limited to CIFAR with ResNet-20, and the geometric alignment assumption is unverified.

oun5uDpuBz.one_liner: Cheap gradient proxies for reasoning models obtained by skipping explicit reasoning or reasoning in continuous latent space.
oun5uDpuBz.problem: Gradient-based optimization of large reasoning models is expensive because gradients must pass through long explicit reasoning traces.
oun5uDpuBz.method: Three proxies use shorter traces: omit explicit reasoning, reason in continuous latent space, or combine the two. Each serves as a replaceable gradient query in data preparation, training, task adaptation, and inference.
oun5uDpuBz.key_idea: Take the gradient through a shorter trace, either no explicit reasoning or distilled latent reasoning, as a stand-in for the gradient through the full chain of thought.
oun5uDpuBz.evidence: Proxy quality and cost (target-loss reduction and cosine similarity per reviews) and four downstream tasks spanning data preparation, training, task adaptation, and inference.
oun5uDpuBz.claimed_gains: No numbers are stated; the abstract claims improved performance with lower computational cost across four tasks.
oun5uDpuBz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the proxies are simple, plug into existing pipelines without changing model structure, and give wall-clock savings across a broad set of tasks.
oun5uDpuBz.main_concern: The proxies compute gradients of different objectives rather than noisy versions of the target gradient, no controls show what the proxy direction contributes, and adaptation and distillation costs and RLVR settings are missing.

qnY84soJSB.one_liner: Online noise optimization for flow matching that rotates source samples with attractive and repulsive forces to straighten trajectories.
qnY84soJSB.problem: Independent noise-data couplings force flow matching to learn curved velocity trajectories that need many function evaluations, and minibatch OT is limited by high-dimensional estimation variance from discrete matching in small batches.
qnY84soJSB.method: Continuous coupling via noise optimization is realized as Spherical Noise Alignment, an online algorithm that rotates source samples through balanced attractive and repulsive forces. It aligns noise with target data during training while preserving prior fidelity, so inference still samples standard Gaussian noise.
qnY84soJSB.key_idea: Rotate noise samples on the sphere under balanced attractive and repulsive forces, with a Gaussian regularizer so inference can still sample the standard Gaussian.
qnY84soJSB.evidence: Experiments on source-target alignment, path curvature, and sample fidelity in few-step (1-4 NFE) sampling, compared mainly with minibatch OT-FM per reviews.
qnY84soJSB.claimed_gains: Improves source-target alignment, significantly reduces path curvature, and gives better sample fidelity in 1-4 NFE sampling, without numbers.
qnY84soJSB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that optimizing noise-data coupling online is a novel and meaningful approach, with a clean spherical decomposition of the Gaussian KL and improved few-step generation.
qnY84soJSB.main_concern: Baselines are limited to minibatch OT-FM, and a training-inference noise-distribution mismatch and kernel-density sample complexity in high dimensions remain unaddressed.

0cQ1F4TUMi.one_liner: Text-to-motion diffusion with dual interaction streams and hand-relative object representations for bimanual one- or two-object manipulation, generated autoregressively.
0cQ1F4TUMi.problem: Existing 4D human-object interaction generation focuses on single-object manipulation and overlooks people coordinating both hands on multiple objects.
0cQ1F4TUMi.method: Dex2HOI processes each object in a dedicated interaction stream coordinated by bidirectional cross-attention, with a Motion Fusion Network, hand-relative object representations, and contact-aware conditioning over the sequence. It samples autoregressively over prefix-conditioned windows without test-time optimization.
0cQ1F4TUMi.key_idea: Run one diffusion stream per object with bidirectional cross-attention, represent objects relative to each hand, and sample long motions autoregressively over prefix-conditioned windows.
0cQ1F4TUMi.evidence: Single- and two-object benchmarks including HIMO, with ablations on FID and penetration (Table 3) per reviews.
0cQ1F4TUMi.claimed_gains: Up to x540 inference speed-up over prior methods, plus improved quantitative results on single- and two-object benchmarks, with no other numbers stated.
0cQ1F4TUMi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified single- and two-object framework addresses a meaningful problem and that the hand-relative representation and dual-stream design help, as shown by ablations.
0cQ1F4TUMi.main_concern: Conceptual novelty over HIMO, InterGen, and similar dual-stream or relative-distance designs is limited, and HIMO comparisons omit recent baselines such as PAMotion and MP-HOI.

mRI6ZexkJz.one_liner: Soft-gates alignment-sensitive distillation losses by the teacher's image-text similarity instead of discarding weakly aligned pairs.
mRI6ZexkJz.problem: Filtering poorly aligned image-text pairs helps pretraining, but in vision-language distillation such pairs still carry useful teacher supervision, so discarding them wastes it.
mRI6ZexkJz.method: AWD computes a per-sample gate from the teacher's image-text similarity that modulates the alignment-sensitive objectives, so well-aligned pairs get stronger contrastive supervision and weakly aligned pairs rely more on the teacher signal. The gate reuses the teacher already used for distillation, adding little overhead.
mRI6ZexkJz.key_idea: Scale only the caption-dependent contrastive losses by the teacher's per-pair image-text similarity while leaving feature, relation, and representation distillation losses unchanged.
mRI6ZexkJz.evidence: CC12M and DataComp-M with CLIP-KD and TIPSv2 distillation, combination with ACID data selection, and ablations on which losses to weight (Table 4) per reviews.
mRI6ZexkJz.claimed_gains: The abstract claims consistent gains over CLIP-KD, complementarity with ACID, and gains on TIPSv2 without numbers; a review cites +3.5 points average on CC12M for CLIP-KD and +3.2 for TIPSv2.
mRI6ZexkJz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the gating is simple and nearly free since teacher embeddings are already computed, and that ablations show weighting only alignment-sensitive losses beats uniform weighting.
mRI6ZexkJz.main_concern: Novelty is a small step from alignment-weighted contrastive methods such as ALIP, results are single runs without variance, and the evidence for splitting the losses is a short ImageNet-only ablation.

dl8KxFkWLD.one_liner: One-round federated graph classification where clients upload diffusion generators and summaries and the server generates, validates, and reweights synthetic graphs.
dl8KxFkWLD.problem: One-shot federated graph learning has focused on node-level tasks, and graph-level classification needs the server to reconstruct reliable graph distributions and reconcile heterogeneous clients without later feedback.
dl8KxFkWLD.method: Clients upload diffusion-based generative knowledge and compact graph distribution summaries once. The server generates synthetic graphs, validates them with structural screening, and reweights them with distribution matching and reliability estimates to reconstruct and fuse client graph distributions.
dl8KxFkWLD.key_idea: Fuse client graph distributions on the server by generating graphs from uploaded diffusion models, filtering them against uploaded structural statistics, and reweighting with constrained distribution matching.
dl8KxFkWLD.evidence: Eight federated graph classification settings, single- and cross-dataset, with component ablations and structural-alignment analyses per reviews.
dl8KxFkWLD.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract excerpt; reviews describe improved accuracy and Macro-F1 in strict one-shot settings.
dl8KxFkWLD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree one-shot federated graph classification is a meaningful problem and that combining graph generation, structural verification, and distribution matching gives promising results across settings.
dl8KxFkWLD.main_concern: The pipeline has many components whose necessity is unclear, communication costs are not quantified, and the client weighting objective and loss-based reliability scores are weakly justified.

Y63UPv1XPS.one_liner: Shows Doob's Lagrangian is asymptotically equivalent to Freidlin-Wentzell quasipotential theory and initializes its control field from the committor.
Y63UPv1XPS.problem: Doob's Lagrangian samples rare transitions without simulating dynamics but is sensitive to initialization and unstable when the transit time T is misspecified.
Y63UPv1XPS.method: The paper proves that minimizing the Doob action over both the control field and T is asymptotically equivalent to computing the quasipotential governing Arrhenius-Kramers rates. It then initializes the control from the stationary committor function and jointly optimizes the control field and T.
Y63UPv1XPS.key_idea: Initialize the Doob control field from the stationary committor, which lies exponentially close in T to the optimal control when one transition channel dominates, and optimize T jointly.
Y63UPv1XPS.evidence: Proofs of the equivalence, of exponential closeness of the initial control, and of stability of joint optimization under a dominant transition channel, plus molecular and toy experiments (ALD and Chignolin per reviews).
Y63UPv1XPS.claimed_gains: not stated; a review says the method lowers estimated energy barriers compared with Doob's Lagrangian on molecular systems.
Y63UPv1XPS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the link between Doob's Lagrangian and Freidlin-Wentzell theory is a novel theoretical contribution that motivates joint optimization of T and committor initialization, with clear presentation.
Y63UPv1XPS.main_concern: Comparisons are limited to Doob's Lagrangian variants without other ML transition-path sampling methods, and it is unclear whether the committor-based scheme scales or holds beyond vanishing noise and a single transition channel.

IpoLpn5DyE.one_liner: Agent builds certified natural-language predicate states as it acts, giving language environments explicit state, mapping, transitions, and termination.
IpoLpn5DyE.problem: Language environments emit raw text and lack the state space, observation-to-state mapping, certified transitions, and termination criterion that MDP analysis needs.
IpoLpn5DyE.method: At each step the agent commits to a natural-language predicate describing how the world should look, takes an action to make it true, and checks the observation against it. Predicates the validator accepts become certified states, and the trajectory records the four missing objects.
IpoLpn5DyE.key_idea: Have the agent construct states predicate by predicate: commit to a predicate, act, and validate the observation against it, so accepted predicates form the task-induced state space.
IpoLpn5DyE.evidence: Five benchmarks spanning planning, scientific exploration, web reasoning, and multi-hop question answering; reviews cite a protocol-phase ablation (Table 6), GPT-4o three-run comparisons, and cost, latency, and injected-verifier-error experiments.
IpoLpn5DyE.claimed_gains: The abstract says SDP achieves the best training-free results on all five benchmarks, with the advantage widening as the horizon grows, without numbers.
IpoLpn5DyE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the protocol separating planning, action, validation, and replanning is clear and gives useful trajectory-level diagnostics, with broad evaluation on five benchmarks.
IpoLpn5DyE.main_concern: Certified states mostly rest on LLM validator judgments rather than environment ground truth, novelty over existing decomposition-and-verification agents is not isolated, and protocol descriptions conflict.

zHTGKi3PtG.one_liner: Closed-form diffusion and flow-matching time schedules from fiberwise optimal-transport prediction risk combined with coefficient-path kinetic action.
zHTGKi3PtG.problem: Kinetic-action schedules motivated by optimal transport are model-agnostic and ignore the predictor's error.
zHTGKi3PtG.method: At a fixed time and state, compatible signal/noise decompositions form an affine fiber, and a fiberwise prediction risk averages optimal-transport costs between true and predictor-induced decompositions. On a fixed coefficient curve, combining this risk with kinetic action gives a closed-form optimal time allocation, with the risk profile estimated from an early baseline checkpoint.
zHTGKi3PtG.key_idea: Allocate sampling time using a prediction-risk profile, the fiberwise OT cost between true and predicted signal/noise decompositions, plus kinetic action, estimated from an early checkpoint.
zHTGKi3PtG.evidence: DDPMs and flow matching across prediction targets, training configurations, risk-estimation checkpoints, datasets, and architectures; a review notes a fixed analytic template retains most gains.
zHTGKi3PtG.claimed_gains: Reduces flow-matching FID by 38.6% on CIFAR-10 at 16 function evaluations.
zHTGKi3PtG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the fiberwise construction is simple and implementable, giving closed-form schedules with improvements across prediction targets, architectures, and training settings.
zHTGKi3PtG.main_concern: The link between the combined objective and actual FID is not established, the comparison ignores the cost of baseline training for risk estimation, and adaptive-schedule baselines are missing.

59GWziSHIl.one_liner: Zero-shot RNA modification site prediction conditioned on molecular descriptors of the modified nucleoside instead of target-specific output heads.
59GWziSHIl.problem: Site annotations are uneven across RNA modification types, and conventional predictors treat modification identity as a fixed supervised label, so they cannot use known molecular identity when site labels are absent.
59GWziSHIl.method: MultiRM is augmented with standardized annotations of complete modified nucleosides, used as molecular side information in a shared compatibility framework. The modification embedding conditions RNA-context selection and final scoring, so one model scores a held-out modification without a target-specific head.
59GWziSHIl.key_idea: Embed the modified nucleoside's chemistry and use it to condition both RNA-context selection and scoring, so unseen modifications are scored by chemical similarity to trained ones.
59GWziSHIl.evidence: Twelve provenance-aware leave-one-modification-out tasks, stricter source-separated and grouped-substructure holdouts, and transfer to ac4C, which is outside the twelve MultiRM modification types.
59GWziSHIl.claimed_gains: The abstract says molecular side information improves zero-shot ranking without numbers; reviews cite a macro AUC gain of +0.019 under leave-one-modification-out, falling to +0.003 under the strict substructure holdout.
59GWziSHIl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the zero-shot setting is practical and the provenance-aware evaluation with several controls is carefully designed.
59GWziSHIl.main_concern: The gain is small and concentrated in chemically similar modifications, shrinking to +0.003 AUC when related substructures are held out, so transfer to novel families is not shown.

e6Vu6BBhmX.one_liner: Time-series domain adaptation using stationary-wavelet intermediate resolutions, with cross-resolution knowledge transfer and committee consensus training.
e6Vu6BBhmX.problem: Time-series domain adaptation methods use only fine temporal or coarse global frequency views and overlook intermediate-resolution structure useful for progressive domain-invariant learning.
e6Vu6BBhmX.method: PRISM builds a resolution hierarchy with the Stationary Wavelet Transform. Cross-Resolution Knowledge Transfer progressively exchanges complementary knowledge across resolutions, and Committee-based Consensus Training bridges the cross-resolution decision hierarchy for more consistent domain-invariant decisions.
e6Vu6BBhmX.key_idea: Wavelet resolutions differ in transferability, discriminability, and per-category decision strength, so exchange knowledge across them and train a committee to reach consensus.
e6Vu6BBhmX.evidence: Six datasets (human activity recognition, fault diagnosis, and sleep staging per reviews) with multiple transfer tasks each, five-seed averages, and empirical analyses of resolution properties with a DANN backbone.
e6Vu6BBhmX.claimed_gains: The abstract says PRISM consistently outperforms existing methods with an average accuracy improvement, but the number is cut off in the excerpt.
e6Vu6BBhmX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is comprehensive across domain types and that the empirical analysis of resolution properties gives a clear rationale for the two modules.
e6Vu6BBhmX.main_concern: The need for the multi-level hierarchy is not shown since four of six datasets use one decomposition level, module synergy is not disentangled, and two baseline rows in Table 1 are numerically identical.

NLc8KJzXBK.one_liner: Protects images from autoregressive editors by perturbing the tokenizer input so selected discrete codewords move farther from the originals.
NLc8KJzXBK.problem: Adversarial protection has targeted diffusion editors, but for autoregressive editors that use discrete visual tokens, changing continuous image features may leave the selected tokens unchanged.
NLc8KJzXBK.method: TokenShield perturbs the image through a frozen image tokenizer under a bounded pixel budget so the protected image selects codewords farther from those of the original, using Ordered Codeword Competition. Candidates are ordered by distance from the original selection and the nearest candidates on either side of each split are compared; no editing instructions or autoregressive decoding are needed.
NLc8KJzXBK.key_idea: Minimize distance gaps between ordered codeword candidates so farther codewords become nearest neighbors, which overcomes quantization hiding continuous perturbations.
NLc8KJzXBK.evidence: Eight image editors across PIE-Bench and Emu Edit, scored with Paired DINO, Paired LPIPS, and Hard-codeword Displacement per reviews; purification robustness is tested only with JPEG.
NLc8KJzXBK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that protecting against discrete-token autoregressive editors is a timely problem, that the continuous-versus-quantized mismatch is clearly identified, and that evaluation covers eight editors on two datasets.
NLc8KJzXBK.main_concern: Larger output differences from the clean edit do not show editing failure, the objective relies on a single frozen LlamaGen tokenizer, and robustness testing covers only JPEG with no adaptive attack.

Jzr4Md86ZI.one_liner: Defines Sleeper Attack: adversarial content planted in agent memory or skills, triggered later, with a 1,896-instance benchmark.
Jzr4Md86ZI.problem: Prior work studies persistent-state threats to LLM agents (memory, reusable skills) one component at a time, with no unified view of cross-interaction attacks.
Jzr4Md86ZI.method: Sleeper Attack is a two-stage process: adversarial content is planted into persistent state, then triggered in a separate interaction. The authors characterize it by attack strategy and persistent-state type and build an LLM-emulated sandbox benchmark (three strategies, three state types, six harm categories).
Jzr4Md86ZI.key_idea: Plant adversarial content in persistent agent state (memory or reusable skills) in one interaction, then trigger it in a later, separate interaction.
Jzr4Md86ZI.evidence: Seven open- and closed-source LLMs on the sandbox benchmark, plus a reproduction in the OpenCode agent framework.
Jzr4Md86ZI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is timely and that the plant-then-trigger formulation gives a useful common framing for memory and skill attacks.
Jzr4Md86ZI.main_concern: Reviewers question whether Sleeper Attack is new or a generalization of existing attacks, and the same-session design leaves planted content visible at trigger time, so persistent state is not isolated.

8CARVyKkMV.one_liner: Adapts an image encoder with causal video self-supervision, then scores planning rollouts by goal-representation consistency.
8CARVyKkMV.problem: Visual world models use frame-wise image representations as prediction targets and planning costs, without temporal context in the representations themselves.
8CARVyKkMV.method: TRIP adapts an image-pretrained encoder with causal video self-supervised learning; a bottleneck adapter matching its prototype distributions supplies targets for a diffusion feature predictor that conditions RGB video generation. For planning, the frozen encoder scores imagined rollouts by comparing the goal's prototype distributions with and without rollout context.
8CARVyKkMV.key_idea: Score a rollout by how much rollout context changes the frozen temporal encoder's prototype distribution of the goal image (goal-representation consistency), needing no cost-specific training.
