FJy46P7d2J.method: Source-MSIS identifies earlier blocking errors from failed trajectories, proposes targeted repairs, replays the task iteratively until completion, and runs an independent verifier that removes subsets of repairs to confirm every remaining intervention is necessary.
FJy46P7d2J.key_idea: Combines counterfactual task replay with an ablation verifier that accepts a repair sequence only if removing any single repair causes failure.
FJy46P7d2J.evidence: Evaluated on three interactive benchmarks (including ALFWorld, Habitat, and ScienceWorld) using Qwen2.5-3B/7B and Gemma3-12B.
FJy46P7d2J.claimed_gains: Source-MSIS achieves an overall recovery success rate of 65.3% compared with 5.7% for the strongest baseline, and reaches 100% on ALFWorld.
FJy46P7d2J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree turning failure attribution into replay-verified executable repairs addresses an important agent-debugging problem.
FJy46P7d2J.main_concern: Baselines score unusually low (<5%) while auxiliary components (parser, action interface) may drive gains, models are small, and post-hoc minimality's practical benefit is unestablished.

DyqClqlrMd.one_liner: Pairs frozen structure-aware protein language models with AlphaFold-trunk MSA features via lightweight probes for out-of-distribution fitness prediction.
DyqClqlrMd.problem: Protein language models suffer severe performance degradation in fitness prediction under distribution shifts such as unseen mutation positions or unseen protein backbones.
DyqClqlrMd.method: The framework combines frozen representations from structure-aware protein language models (e.g., ESM-3, SaProt) with pooled features from an AlphaFold-style trunk run on each sequence and its MSA. A lightweight MLP prediction probe maps these combined representations to fitness scores.
DyqClqlrMd.key_idea: Fusing frozen structure-aware pLM embeddings with AlphaFold-trunk MSA features through a lightweight probe to study modality generalization under shifts.
DyqClqlrMd.evidence: Evaluated on the FLIP2 fitness-landscape benchmark across held-out mutation position and held-out protein backbone distribution shifts.
DyqClqlrMd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating fitness predictors under practical OOD shifts and disentangling structural versus co-evolutionary contributions yields useful scientific findings.
DyqClqlrMd.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty, unmatched probe feature normalization between pLM-only and pLM+trunk comparisons, missing uncertainty estimates in main results, and no single selectable configuration across shifts.

qv0mmJboD6.one_liner: Simulates recommender users with a three-dimensional psychological latent state aligned to real interaction logs via Unbalanced Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport.
qv0mmJboD6.problem: Current LLM-based user simulators act as short-term surface imitators that fail to model long-horizon dynamics like fatigue, affect, and shifting preferences.
qv0mmJboD6.method: PsyBer-Agent models each user with three evolving latent states via Psy-Engine and aligns log-conditioned reference trajectories with simulated trajectories using Unbalanced Gromov-Wasserstein (UGW) optimal transport to train a lightweight policy without fine-tuning the backbone LLM. The authors also introduce the WebSim platform and PsyBer Benchmark.
qv0mmJboD6.key_idea: Aligning three-dimensional psychological latent-state trajectories to real user logs via Unbalanced Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport to supervise a lightweight simulator policy.
qv0mmJboD6.evidence: Evaluated on WebSim and the PsyBer Benchmark across shopping and web-browsing scenarios, seven recommender backbones, and up to 5M queued simulation tasks.
qv0mmJboD6.claimed_gains: Maintains stable performance under large-scale concurrent simulation for up to 5M queued simulation tasks.
qv0mmJboD6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling dynamic user states with offline log alignment and building the scalable WebSim simulation platform are practically useful.
qv0mmJboD6.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments do not isolate the psychological state design from generic latent states, validation horizons (10 rounds) are short, and HR@10/NDCG@10 on replayed slates inadequately measure human-simulator agreement.

N9lAN4cQVu.one_liner: Amortizes RL task-generator training by replacing online solver rollouts with a frozen-reference activation probe predicting target solve rate.
N9lAN4cQVu.problem: Training RL task generators to produce frontier-difficulty problems requires prohibitively expensive repeated solver rollouts for every candidate task, especially in software engineering.
N9lAN4cQVu.method: PROPEL trains a lightweight activation probe on a one-time labeled corpus of generated tasks and solver outcomes using representations from a frozen generator reference model, then uses the probe as a single-forward-pass proxy reward during generator RL.
N9lAN4cQVu.key_idea: Replaces online solver rollouts in task-generator RL with a lightweight activation probe over a frozen generator reference model trained once to predict target-solver pass rates.
N9lAN4cQVu.evidence: Evaluated across math, coding, and software-engineering tasks at multiple model scales, including Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct coding solvers.
N9lAN4cQVu.claimed_gains: For coding, tasks generated at the learnable frontier increase from 10.1% to 20.0% for a Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct solver.
N9lAN4cQVu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree PROPEL targets a real computational bottleneck in solver-in-the-loop task generation and credibly demonstrates amortization benefits across domains.
N9lAN4cQVu.main_concern: Reviewers warn that a static probe trained on base-generator outputs is vulnerable to distribution shift and reward hacking during RL (especially with a weak SWE probe) and leaves downstream solver learning gains unvalidated.

Ykvl1racQI.one_liner: Measures LLM reasoning bias via cued-minus-uncued hidden-state displacement geometry (coherence and participation ratio) and counterfactual twin distillation.
Ykvl1racQI.problem: Reasoning biases are often targeted with single steering vectors without knowing whether the underlying hidden-state shifts share a common direction across inputs.
Ykvl1racQI.method: The authors patch answer-position hidden states from cued runs into uncued twins to locate layer crossovers, summarize cued-minus-uncued displacement geometry via participation ratio and mean-shift coherence, and propose an input-adaptive correction using counterfactual twin distillation.
Ykvl1racQI.key_idea: Quantifies cued-minus-uncued hidden-state shift geometry via participation ratio and coherence to diagnose when shared steering vectors fail and motivate counterfactual twin distillation.
Ykvl1racQI.evidence: Evaluated across seven direct-answer checkpoints (7B–70B, base and MoE) and nine paired-prompt datasets including cognitive-bias corpora, MMLU option-position, and 11 BBQ categories.
Ykvl1racQI.claimed_gains: Even the best shared additive offset removes less than 13% of the displacement energy in either pooled cognitive-bias corpus.
Ykvl1racQI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the two-run formulation and the (coherence, participation ratio) diagnostic plane simple and informative for explaining why steering vectors fail on cognitive biases.
Ykvl1racQI.main_concern: Reviewers point to severe dataset-construction confounds between cued and uncued twins, conflation of diverse behaviors as biases, and weak causal support in registered tests.

gs3uNjP4sJ.one_liner: Learns conditional expert-reward distributions from sparse expert labels and abundant implicit feedback via doubly robust kernel mean embeddings.
gs3uNjP4sJ.problem: RLHF reward models rely on costly explicit expert preferences or noisy implicit feedback and collapse preference variation into a single scalar expectation.
gs3uNjP4sJ.method: Reward Conditional Mean Embedding (RCME) uses a characteristic kernel and a doubly robust, Neyman-orthogonal estimator to learn conditional expert-reward distributions from sparse expert supervision and abundant implicit feedback, integrated into policy optimization via Group Kernel Relative Policy Optimization (GKRPO).
gs3uNjP4sJ.key_idea: Estimates conditional expert-reward distributions with a doubly robust Neyman-orthogonal kernel mean embedding and optimizes policies via kernel alignment to a maximum-reward anchor.
gs3uNjP4sJ.evidence: Identification and Neyman-orthogonality theory plus empirical validation on synthetic, semi-synthetic, and safety-alignment tasks.
gs3uNjP4sJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the setting of combining sparse expert supervision with biased implicit feedback is practically relevant and cleanly formalized with a doubly robust orthogonal estimator.
gs3uNjP4sJ.main_concern: Reviewers note that GKRPO collapses the learned distribution back into a single expected transformed reward before policy updates, that the missing-at-random assumption may fail in practice, and that exposition is hard to follow.

i1Eq9KR2Rj.one_liner: Distills expert-guided text refinements into minimal deletion-only programs to train a scalable LLM pretraining data refiner.
i1Eq9KR2Rj.problem: Document-level pretraining data filtering is too coarse, whereas directly prompting teachers to emit executable editing programs limits refinement quality and efficiency.
i1Eq9KR2Rj.method: RefineX extracts minimal edit-based deletion programs from expert-guided end-to-end text refinements and distills them into a compact refinement model (Qwen3-0.6B) that performs fine-grained, deletion-only corpus cleaning at scale.
i1Eq9KR2Rj.key_idea: Distills expert-guided end-to-end text refinements into minimal deletion-only editing programs to train a compact refiner for large-scale pretraining corpora.
i1Eq9KR2Rj.evidence: Evaluated via from-scratch pretraining at multiple model scales (including 750M) across ten downstream lighteval tasks against raw, filtered, and ProX-refined corpora.
i1Eq9KR2Rj.claimed_gains: On the 750M model, RefineX yields 2.6%–7.2% average gains on lighteval tasks.
i1Eq9KR2Rj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like decoupling teacher text refinement from program extraction, using inspectable deletion-only edits, and validating with actual from-scratch pretraining.
i1Eq9KR2Rj.main_concern: Reviewers point out an uncontrolled capacity confound versus ProX (0.6B vs. 0.3B refiner), that deletion-only edits can still alter semantics (e.g., dropping negations), and that difflib does not guarantee minimum Levenshtein edits.

8cPNtV8hya.one_liner: Curates a four-capability K-12 instruction corpus and fine-tunes open 4B, 9B, and 27B educational foundation models.
8cPNtV8hya.problem: Existing educational LLMs specialize in either problem solving or tutoring because their training mixtures are organized by data source rather than balanced across core teaching capabilities.
8cPNtV8hya.method: OmniEdu combines over 100 educational and general sources through deterministic cleaning, LLM semantic auditing/rewriting, quality scoring, diversity selection, and pedagogical instruction assignment into 69,999 examples (15.96M response tokens) spanning subject competence, curriculum grounding, diagnostic reasoning, and scaffolding, then fine-tunes 4B, 9B, and 27B models.
8cPNtV8hya.key_idea: Organizes multi-source K-12 instruction curation around four explicit educational capabilities—subject competence, curriculum grounding, diagnostic reasoning, and pedagogical scaffolding.
8cPNtV8hya.evidence: Fine-tuned 4B, 9B, and 27B models evaluated on curriculum-grounding, K-12 problem-solving, pedagogical-tutoring, and general capability benchmarks.
8cPNtV8hya.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value releasing open educational models and evaluating across complementary capabilities beyond subject QA across three model scales.
8cPNtV8hya.main_concern: Reviewers note that comparisons against untuned base models fail to isolate the data-curation pipeline's individual components and raise contamination concerns due to overlapping training and benchmark sources.

oNRniV3HWY.one_liner: Trains multi-class classifiers from unlabeled data, incompletely revealed same-class pairs, and class priors using a one-sided reveal likelihood.
oNRniV3HWY.problem: Treating unrevealed pairs as negative different-class relations biases multi-class classifiers trained from incomplete same-class pairwise supervision.
oNRniV3HWY.method: PRIME models the probability that a pair is revealed under a class-independent one-sided reveal process via the latent classifier's induced same-class similarity and adds a permutation-invariant class-prior regularizer to prevent marginal collapse.
oNRniV3HWY.key_idea: Combines a one-sided incomplete-similarity reveal likelihood with a permutation-invariant class-prior regularizer to recover multi-class classifiers up to permutation from positive pairs and unlabeled data.
oNRniV3HWY.evidence: Population recovery proofs, uniform finite-sample generalization bounds, and experiments on five image classification benchmarks (MNIST, FashionMNIST, KMNIST, CIFAR10, STL10).
oNRniV3HWY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean modeling distinction between unrevealed and negative pairs supported by population-recovery and generalization theory.
oNRniV3HWY.main_concern: Reviewers question the restrictive class-independent one-sided reveal and known-prior assumptions, synthetic-only benchmark validation, and missing adapted PU/weak-supervision baselines.

mf6dyte2oK.one_liner: Restores real old photos mask-free by freezing early 1–2 step edit-response fields into RoPE modulation and optimizing with no-reference GRPO.
mf6dyte2oK.problem: Restoring real faded old photographs without clean ground-truth references or damage masks is hard for supervised fine-tuning alone.
mf6dyte2oK.method: EMBER extracts a Gated 1–2 Step Edit-Response Field (G12) from a pretrained image editor's first two denoising steps, freezes it into mask-free rotary-phase modulation, and adapts the editor on real old photographs via no-reference GRPO.
mf6dyte2oK.key_idea: Freezes early 1–2 step denoising edit responses into mask-free rotary-phase modulation and optimizes restoration quality on real photos using no-reference GRPO.
mf6dyte2oK.evidence: Evaluated on GGT-100K OldPhoto with learned non-reward metrics, NIQE, fixed-weight causal interventions, and a blinded human study (48 photos, 31 participants).
mf6dyte2oK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the realistic mask-free real-photo restoration setting, the blinded human evaluation, and the concept of reusing early denoising trajectories.
mf6dyte2oK.main_concern: Reviewers point out that fixed-checkpoint interventions show no significant LPIPS benefit from correct versus permuted G12 spatial fields, leaving G12's restoration benefit unproven alongside incremental novelty.

lxGrzU1x9c.one_liner: Trains reasoning models to recover from corrupted chain-of-thought prefixes via privileged on-policy self-distillation using dual teacher signals.
lxGrzU1x9c.problem: Unsafe intermediate chain-of-thought steps can steer an otherwise safe language model's subsequent reasoning toward harmful assistance.
lxGrzU1x9c.method: ImmuneCoT exposes a student model to corrupted reasoning prefixes and distills token-level targets from a frozen same-model teacher providing both a prefix-conditioned Recognition signal and a prefix-bypassing Response signal. A base-adjusted product of experts fuses these signals on-policy, paired with auxiliary benign examples for self-tolerance.
lxGrzU1x9c.key_idea: Fuses prefix-conditioned Recognition and prefix-bypassing Response teacher distributions via a base-adjusted product of experts to supervise on-policy student continuations from corrupted prefixes.
lxGrzU1x9c.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B across standard safety, over-refusal, and general-capability benchmarks, plus Qwen3-4B under H-CoT mid-reasoning hijacking.
lxGrzU1x9c.claimed_gains: Among initially safe cases under H-CoT hijacking, ImmuneCoT achieves a 55.5% safe recovery rate and a 26.1 percentage-point paired advantage over STAR-1 on the shared Clean-safe subset.
lxGrzU1x9c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that training models to recover from mid-reasoning safety drift targets a meaningful gap and is evaluated broadly alongside utility.
lxGrzU1x9c.main_concern: Multiple reviewers note that 80 of 106 safe infected outcomes simply terminate the thinking block immediately rather than repairing reasoning, and ablations do not cleanly isolate signal complementarity.

RNdYnbqaXF.one_liner: Trains a coarse-to-fine scRNA-seq cell-type annotation LLM agent with SFT, RL, and a self-evolving skill bank distilled from rollouts.
RNdYnbqaXF.problem: Existing LLM-based scRNA-seq cell-type annotators rely on fixed prompting workflows that neither adapt actions to intermediate observations nor reuse successful strategies across datasets.
RNdYnbqaXF.method: HiCellS casts hierarchical cell-type annotation as a learnable sequential agent task that observes clustering outputs, marker evidence, and biological knowledge to choose refinement actions. It initializes the agent via supervised fine-tuning, optimizes actions with reinforcement learning using final accuracy feedback, and distills rollout trajectories into reusable skills.
RNdYnbqaXF.key_idea: Co-evolves a reinforcement-learned hierarchical annotation agent with a skill bank distilled from rollout trajectories to adapt clustering and marker-interpretation actions.
RNdYnbqaXF.evidence: Evaluated across diverse scRNA-seq datasets and multiple tissues with component ablations on RL and skill evolution plus failure-case analyses.
RNdYnbqaXF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying clustering and hierarchical cell-type annotation with RL and evolving skills reflects practical workflows and includes informative ablations and failure analyses.
RNdYnbqaXF.main_concern: Multiple reviewers flag an unfair evaluation where HiCellS is scored only on cells retained after its own quality filtering while baselines are evaluated without that filtering.

ahV3HzSSET.one_liner: Merges LoRA experts via layer-importance attenuation, lightweight input-dependent expert routing, and asymmetric layer-wise integration.
ahV3HzSSET.problem: Existing model merging methods combine complete task updates or weight whole experts uniformly, ignoring uneven LoRA layer contributions and causing parameter conflicts and cross-task interference.
ahV3HzSSET.method: Merging What Matters (MWM) first identifies task-critical LoRA updates per expert and attenuates auxiliary updates, then uses a lightweight router to select input-relevant experts. Finally, it integrates selected experts with differentiated layer-wise rules that preserve the primary expert's core layers while conservatively merging complementary updates.
ahV3HzSSET.key_idea: Combines per-expert LoRA layer-importance attenuation, input-conditioned expert routing, and asymmetric layer-wise merging rules to protect primary-expert core layers.
ahV3HzSSET.evidence: Evaluated across natural language processing and computer vision benchmarks against more than 15 merging baselines and task-specific fine-tuned experts, including out-of-domain generalization and component ablations.
ahV3HzSSET.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing interference into layer importance, input routing, and asymmetric integration is well motivated and backed by broad NLP and CV experiments.
ahV3HzSSET.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty relative to existing dynamic and layer-aware merging or MoE methods such as WEMoE and MoW-Merging, and note unvalidated stability of layer selection and routing.

9IhYTqoSLP.one_liner: Localizes forecast-relevant hidden states in time-series foundation models via mutual information and uses them to guide retrieval in ANCHOR-RAG.
9IhYTqoSLP.problem: Output accuracy alone does not reveal which internal hidden representations time-series foundation models rely on for forecasting or whether those signals are functionally meaningful.
9IhYTqoSLP.method: Information Anchors computes mutual information between hidden representations and future targets across layers and temporal positions, validated with representation probing and activation interventions. The authors further introduce ANCHOR-RAG, which uses a history-only mutual-information anchor signal to guide retrieval and integration of historical evidence.
9IhYTqoSLP.key_idea: Uses mutual information between hidden states and future targets to localize forecast-relevant temporal anchor regions and guide history-only retrieval in time-series foundation models.
9IhYTqoSLP.evidence: Evaluated across 42 mutual-information atlases spanning six heterogeneous time-series foundation models and seven data regimes, plus ANCHOR-RAG forecasting experiments across seven datasets.
9IhYTqoSLP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that localizing forecast-relevant internal representations across diverse time-series foundation model architectures is an interesting question supported by broad empirical sweeps.
9IhYTqoSLP.main_concern: Reviewers question the necessity and stability of mutual information—citing low block-resampling reselection rates, small MI-specific gains in ANCHOR-RAG, and a fragmented narrative.

DLOUGy0vS5.one_liner: Accelerates scene-aware human motion synthesis to one or few steps via a jointly trained global-to-local shortcut model.
DLOUGy0vS5.problem: Existing scene-aware human motion synthesis methods rely on slow multi-step diffusion sampling with high runtime latency.
DLOUGy0vS5.method: SceShortcut uses a two-stage global-to-local shortcut architecture trained end-to-end: the global stage predicts intermediate motion features and a coarse root transport velocity to query local dense height-field geometry, which the local stage uses to predict remaining motion velocities and a root residual correction. Training adds combined root-transport-velocity supervision and root-residual regularization.
DLOUGy0vS5.key_idea: Predicts coarse global root velocity within each shortcut step to query local height-field geometry for predicting body velocities and a regularized root residual.
DLOUGy0vS5.evidence: Evaluated on TRUMANS and HUMANISE benchmarks with one-step and few-step sampling and architectural and root-supervision ablations.
DLOUGy0vS5.claimed_gains: On TRUMANS and HUMANISE, one-step sampling with SceShortcut achieves approximately 50-100x speedup over diffusion baselines.
DLOUGy0vS5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize efficient scene-aware motion generation as a meaningful problem and find the within-step global-to-local design intuitive with strong speedups.
DLOUGy0vS5.main_concern: Reviewers question baseline comparison fairness and runtime reporting, note missing motion diversity metrics for one-step generation, and ask for clearer attribution beyond existing shortcut modeling.

7jQ6t9WBLK.one_liner: Adapts LLM reasoning accuracy and verbalized confidence at test time using self-supervised RL signals derived from multi-sample response frequencies.
7jQ6t9WBLK.problem: Supervised RL calibration methods require ground-truth labels and degrade under domain shift, limiting calibration adaptation on unlabeled target tasks.
7jQ6t9WBLK.method: Test-Time Calibration Learning (TTCL) samples multiple model responses on unlabeled target-task inputs to derive continuous self-supervision targets for both answer correctness and verbalized confidence. It jointly optimizes both objectives with RL and provides a theoretical bound linking TTCL to the ideal calibration objective.
7jQ6t9WBLK.key_idea: Derives continuous self-supervised correctness and confidence targets from multi-sample response frequencies to jointly optimize accuracy and verbalized calibration via test-time RL.
7jQ6t9WBLK.evidence: Provides a bounded-surrogate theoretical analysis and experiments on mathematical reasoning and factual QA benchmarks across multiple LLMs including domain-shift settings.
7jQ6t9WBLK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that label-free test-time calibration under domain shift is a practical problem and that separating answer and confidence rewards with soft frequency targets is reasonable.
7jQ6t9WBLK.main_concern: Reviewers point out that frequent answers can be wrong (reinforcing overconfident errors), test-time RL adapts and evaluates on the same test set at high sampling cost, and reported NQ ECE values contain an arithmetic inconsistency.

nHHdMcZadW.one_liner: Stabilizes agentic RL by permissively screening degenerate rollouts and clipping excessive per-trajectory gradient norms before batch aggregation.
nHHdMcZadW.problem: Multi-turn tool-integrated RL suffers training collapse, while binary trajectory filtering leaves retained trajectories with huge gradients uncontrolled.
nHHdMcZadW.method: TIER introduces a three-level trajectory intervention combining permissive response-level screening to discard clearly degenerate rollouts with per-trajectory gradient norm clipping before batch aggregation that preserves update direction. This discards degenerate rollouts, attenuates overly influential ones, and fully retains normal trajectories.
nHHdMcZadW.key_idea: Combines permissive response-statistic screening for degenerate rollouts with direction-preserving per-trajectory gradient clipping prior to batch aggregation.
nHHdMcZadW.evidence: Evaluated on six mathematical reasoning benchmarks with code interpreters and a Search-R1 QA setting using Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-4B-Base, plus controller ablations.
nHHdMcZadW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple, intuitive, and supported by consistent math benchmark improvements and thorough ablations.
nHHdMcZadW.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty beyond heuristic filtering plus per-example gradient clipping, narrow non-math agentic evaluation, and weak causal diagnosis of extreme gradient spikes.

gxsosiK6mK.one_liner: Revitalizes single-timestep convolutional SNNs using multi-threshold parallel neurons, convolutional global-local aggregation, and dilated multi-scale position encoding.
gxsosiK6mK.problem: Convolutional SNNs lag behind spiking Transformers in representational capacity, while Transformer attention complicates asynchronous neuromorphic deployment.
gxsosiK6mK.method: MTA-SNN augments convolutional SNNs with three neuromorphic-friendly primitives: Multi-Threshold Parallel Neurons (MTPN) with shared weights and heterogeneous firing thresholds across channels, Global Local Aggregation (GLA) using depthwise convolutions and global pooling, and Multi-Scale Position Encoding (MSPE) via dilated convolutions.
gxsosiK6mK.key_idea: Replaces multi-step temporal integration and attention with shared-weight multi-threshold parallel neurons, pooling-based global-local aggregation, and dilated-convolution positional encoding.
gxsosiK6mK.evidence: Evaluated at single timestep (T=1) on CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet with module ablations and hardware deployment on a Speck2e neuromorphic chip.
gxsosiK6mK.claimed_gains: Achieves 83.07% accuracy on CIFAR-100 and 78.37% on ImageNet with a single timestep.
gxsosiK6mK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge strong single-timestep classification accuracy and a hardware-friendly convolutional design validated on Speck2e.
gxsosiK6mK.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty relative to prior multi-threshold SNNs and CNN attention modules, and point out inconsistent numbers across tables and unfair or broken baseline comparisons.

DXa50wgJNp.one_liner: Partitions representational agreement among time-series foundation models into input-kernel similarity and a residual beyond input histories.
DXa50wgJNp.problem: It is unclear whether pretrained time-series foundation models share genuinely learned temporal representations or merely reflect input-history geometry.
DXa50wgJNp.method: The paper compares linear hidden-state similarity (CKA) across pretrained time-series models against architecture-matched random initializations, decomposing the pretraining agreement gain into an input-kernel reference component and an orthogonal residual. It further tests depth, family deletions, ordinary forecast supervision, and input transformations.
DXa50wgJNp.key_idea: Decomposes pretrained-versus-initialized CKA agreement across time-series models into an input-history kernel span and an orthogonal representational residual.
DXa50wgJNp.evidence: Analyzes 10 model variants from 7 model families across 17 datasets with controls for depth, family deletion, ordinary forecasting, and downstream decision rules.
DXa50wgJNp.claimed_gains: At the last observed position and final recorded depth, about 27% of the pretraining agreement increase remains outside the input-kernel reference.
DXa50wgJNp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the careful experimental scope, targeted controls, and evidence cautioning against equating representational similarity with forecasting utility.
DXa50wgJNp.main_concern: Reviewers note that the paper fails to identify what temporal properties the residual actually encodes or provide concrete guidance for pretraining or forecasting.

TiGFnzNnZW.one_liner: Injects evaluation rubrics during failed RL rollouts to repair agent trajectories and filters high-shift samples for policy updates.
TiGFnzNnZW.problem: On-policy agentic RL stalls when tasks exceed the current policy's capability boundary, yielding sparse or zero successful trajectories.
TiGFnzNnZW.method: Rollout-Time Intervention (RTI) triggers only on all-failed rollout groups, using reward-side evaluation rubrics via validator and corrector roles to convert erroneous trajectories into successful ones. Trajectories with excessive distributional shift are filtered out before standard GRPO policy updates.
TiGFnzNnZW.key_idea: Repairs all-failed rollout groups using evaluation rubrics during rollout generation and filters out high-shift intervened trajectories before GRPO updates.
TiGFnzNnZW.evidence: Evaluated across five benchmarks (including Hard20 and Rest-OOD) with Qwen3-8B/9B backbones and filtering ablations.
TiGFnzNnZW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical motivation, clean intervention trigger on all-zero groups without altering GRPO, and strong empirical gains over GRPO.
TiGFnzNnZW.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the injection of privileged ground-truth/rubric information during rollouts without matching teacher/hint baselines (e.g., Guide-GRPO, ExPO) or ablating the three-role pipeline.

CnG68VRdPZ.one_liner: Routes global, local, and text-only evidence using quantized and continuous image-text alignment priors for multimodal manipulation detection.
CnG68VRdPZ.problem: Multimodal manipulation detectors aggregate cross-modal features without conditioning fusion on each sample's image-text alignment regime.
CnG68VRdPZ.method: SAFE-Align quantizes global image-text similarity into a discrete alignment state embedding combined with continuous similarity as a routing prior that weights global-interaction, local-spatial, and text-only evidence. It also models bidirectional patch-token correspondence to capture local agreement and discrepancy cues for grounding.
CnG68VRdPZ.key_idea: Combines a quantized alignment-state embedding and continuous image-text similarity as a routing prior to weight global, local-spatial, and text-only manipulation evidence.
CnG68VRdPZ.evidence: Evaluated on the official DGM4 split across four tasks with fusion and component ablations averaged over three runs.
CnG68VRdPZ.claimed_gains: On DGM4, SAFE-Align reaches 95.63% AUC, 88.74% accuracy, and 89.63% mAP (improving over ASAP by 1.25, 1.03, and 1.10 points) and beats uniform fusion by 1.55 AUC and an unconditioned gate by 1.97 AUC.
CnG68VRdPZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating semantic alignment from authenticity to condition evidence routing is well-motivated and improves classification metrics on DGM4.
CnG68VRdPZ.main_concern: Reviewers note evaluation is limited to a single dataset (DGM4) with weaker grounding metrics, imported baseline numbers, and unisolated routing versus direct alignment-feature injection.

T2hvhKDhKr.one_liner: Evaluates long-video MLLMs on locating, linking, and combining distributed needles using paired main and diagnostic sub-question chains.
T2hvhKDhKr.problem: Final-answer accuracy on long-video benchmarks hides whether MLLMs actually locate, link, and synthesize distributed intermediate evidence.
T2hvhKDhKr.method: ThreadNIAH defines five task types across three reasoning levels (Single-Needle Retrieval, Multi-Needle Threading, Multi-Needle Synthesis) instantiated via 29 templates into 870 QA chains pairing each Main QA with diagnostic Sub-QAs. It measures Main Acc, Sub Acc, and All Pass Rate (APR) across full chains.
T2hvhKDhKr.key_idea: Pairs controlled multi-needle long-video questions with diagnostic sub-questions in QA chains, scoring full-chain All Pass Rate to expose hidden reasoning failures.
T2hvhKDhKr.evidence: Comprises 870 Main QAs and 2,580 Sub-QAs evaluated across frontier and open-weight MLLMs with prefix-survival and natural-video correlation analyses.
T2hvhKDhKr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the locate/link/combine taxonomy and the QA-chain APR diagnostic for exposing large gaps hidden by final-answer accuracy.
T2hvhKDhKr.main_concern: Reviewers flag an uncontrolled frame-sampling confound on hour-long videos, heavy reliance on synthetic overlaid symbols rather than natural video events, and model-biased QA generation/auditing.

tJ7GAPAnyH.one_liner: Identifies and removes harmful image or text components within multimodal in-context demonstrations via leave-one-component-out counterfactual inference.
tJ7GAPAnyH.problem: Whole multimodal demonstrations that appear helpful overall can contain an individual image or text component that harms the query prediction.
tJ7GAPAnyH.method: Selective Counterfactual Component Intervention (SCCI) is a training-free method that splits each in-context demonstration into visual and textual components and runs leave-one-component-out inference to compute counterfactual self-log-likelihood signals. A reliability-aware decision rule removes a component only when evidence is sufficiently informative.
tJ7GAPAnyH.key_idea: Runs leave-one-component-out inference over visual and textual demonstration parts and selectively prunes components using a confidence-based counterfactual reliability rule.
tJ7GAPAnyH.evidence: Evaluated on 4-shot MICL across six vision-language benchmarks using Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL2.5-8B against unmodified, random, and whole-demonstration removal baselines.
tJ7GAPAnyH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formalizing hidden component harm in non-atomic multimodal demonstrations is a precise and interesting observation.
tJ7GAPAnyH.main_concern: Reviewers point out that SCCI incurs ~8x inference cost for marginal gains and lacks compute-matched best-of-9 controls to verify gains come from component removal rather than confidence-based answer selection.

82cRU1SgNd.one_liner: Generates physically responsive videos under camera-space 3D force control using projective 3D force maps and depth-grounded response supervision.
82cRU1SgNd.problem: Direct force-controlled video generators rely on 2D image-plane forces that cannot represent camera-space 3D forces or local 3D response geometry.
82cRU1SgNd.method: ForceVid3D conditions a pretrained video DiT (Wan) on a Projective 3D Force Map encoding force support, direction, magnitude, and projection cues from an initial image. During training, Depth-Grounded Response Affinity Supervision (D-RAS) combines response-affinity and local relative-depth objectives, trained on a new 60K-pair ForceVid3D-Dataset.
82cRU1SgNd.key_idea: Conditions video generation on a Projective 3D Force Map and supervises training with joint response-affinity and local relative-depth losses.
82cRU1SgNd.evidence: Introduces the 60K-pair ForceVid3D-Dataset across seven response groups and ForceVid3D-Bench, evaluated under 2D and 3D force-control settings with ablations.
82cRU1SgNd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that camera-space 3D force control is a practically relevant extension and value the accompanying 60K synthetic dataset and benchmark.
82cRU1SgNd.main_concern: Reviewers note that baselines are not retrained on ForceVid3D-Dataset (confounding comparisons), automatic 3D evaluation covers very few cases without 3D baselines, and D-RAS objectives are not individually ablated.

KlfVWfhiKc.one_liner: Regularizes multimodal autonomous driving planners by calibrating candidate trajectory diversity in action-conditioned predictive latent space.
KlfVWfhiKc.problem: Multimodal driving planners generate geometrically distinct candidate trajectories that often induce redundant future evolutions, wasting the candidate budget.
KlfVWfhiKc.method: AMC-Drive passes candidate trajectories through an action-conditioned predictive representation (JEPA-style world model) to measure affinity over induced future evolutions rather than raw trajectory geometry. It defines a differentiable effective multimodality measure to consolidate redundant modes during training without changing inference.
KlfVWfhiKc.key_idea: Measures and regularizes candidate trajectory redundancy via pairwise affinities in an action-conditioned predictive world-model latent space during training.
KlfVWfhiKc.evidence: Evaluated on NAVSIM v1 and NAVSIM v2 with proposal-, diffusion-, and flow-based planners and component ablations.
KlfVWfhiKc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing geometric trajectory diversity from distinct induced futures is a well-posed problem with a clean training-only formulation.
KlfVWfhiKc.main_concern: Reviewers note that most gains appear to come from the frozen predictive backbone rather than AMC itself, and the paper lacks direct metrics (e.g., coverage or Keff comparisons) proving improved effective multimodality.

HMot1JfjcK.one_liner: Trains a small RL concept generator to emit diverse problem-specific strategies that steer a larger frozen LLM's solution exploration.
HMot1JfjcK.problem: Naive repeated sampling for LLM test-time scaling relies on local decoding noise and produces near-duplicate attempts on hard reasoning tasks.
HMot1JfjcK.method: A small concept-generator LLM is trained with reinforcement learning to emit diverse problem-specific concepts, hints, or strategies in a single trajectory to maximize the downstream success of a larger frozen answer generator. The learned search policy can then steer unseen larger answer generators at test time.
HMot1JfjcK.key_idea: Optimizes a small LLM with RL to generate diverse semantic strategy concepts that condition and steer a larger frozen solver's test-time sampling.
HMot1JfjcK.evidence: Evaluated on hard mathematical reasoning benchmarks (DeepMath, Omni-MATH 2) using Qwen2.5 and Llama-3.3 backbones, including cross-family transfer tests.
HMot1JfjcK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value that a small trained concept generator improves a frozen larger solver and transfers across model families without updating solver weights.
HMot1JfjcK.main_concern: Reviewers cite narrow, outdated benchmarks and models, reliance on Qwen2.5-32B as an unverified judge for both training rewards and evaluation, and lack of compute-matched learned-guidance baselines.

q6I0JIQrgS.one_liner: Scores candidate textual skills via outcome-aware likelihood comparisons on verified trajectories to selectively inject skills during agentic RL.
q6I0JIQrgS.problem: Skill-based agentic RL assumes injected skills always help or relies on costly, noisy environment rollouts to estimate skill utility.
q6I0JIQrgS.method: SkillScaffold reuses outcome-verified training trajectories to generate candidate textual skills and estimate policy-relative skill utility via outcome-aware likelihood comparisons without extra rollouts. It selectively injects helpful skills or abstains, jointly training the skill Generator and Executor while encouraging skill-free inference.
q6I0JIQrgS.key_idea: Estimates policy-relative textual skill utility via outcome-aware likelihood comparisons on reused verified trajectories to gate selective skill injection during RL.
q6I0JIQrgS.evidence: Evaluated on ALFWorld, WebShop, ScienceWorld, and a fourth long-horizon benchmark using Qwen3-8B, with ablations on selection, abstention, and generator training.
q6I0JIQrgS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical selective-injection framing, low-cost trajectory reuse without inference-time skill overhead, and consistent benchmark improvements.
q6I0JIQrgS.main_concern: Reviewers note narrow methodological novelty beyond the likelihood utility score, unvalidated behavior when all scout rollouts fail, single-backbone evaluation (Qwen3-8B), and missing wall-clock compute comparisons.

2luWLnXnGZ.one_liner: Solves distributed nonconvex learning with affine coupling over directed networks via push-sum residual tracking, gradient smoothing, and moving-center regularization.
2luWLnXnGZ.problem: Distributed nonconvex stochastic optimization with global affine coupling constraints over unbalanced directed networks cannot evaluate global feasibility locally.
2luWLnXnGZ.method: DiSPART (Directed Stochastic Primal-dual Algorithm with Residual Tracking) converts global affine constraints into distributed feedback by combining push-sum residual and multiplier tracking with gradient smoothing and moving-center regularization in a single communication round per step.
2luWLnXnGZ.key_idea: Combines push-sum residual and multiplier tracking with gradient smoothing and moving-center regularization to enforce affine coupling over directed networks.
2luWLnXnGZ.evidence: Proves finite-time expected squared KKT residual bounds under smoothness and Perron-weighted mixing, accompanied by synthetic and real-data classification experiments (a9a, Multiple Features).
2luWLnXnGZ.claimed_gains: Establishes O(K^{-1/2}) convergence on average expected squared KKT residual with stochastic gradients and O(K^{-1}) with exact gradients for fixed problem and network parameters.
2luWLnXnGZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge the challenging combination of nonconvexity, affine coupling, and directed unbalanced networks with a technically solid convergence analysis.
2luWLnXnGZ.main_concern: Reviewers highlight missing experimental specifications for the real-data tasks (objectives, models, coupling constraints) and unclear or mismatched convergence-rate comparisons against convex-only baselines.

5zceymhFF7.one_liner: Accelerates few-step video DiTs without retraining by interleaving sparse latent-frame subsets across transformer blocks.
5zceymhFF7.problem: Step-wise caching and reuse methods yield diminishing speedups in few-step distilled video Diffusion Transformers due to sparse denoising steps.
5zceymhFF7.method: FIS-DiT shifts acceleration from the denoising trajectory to the latent-frame dimension by executing Frame Interleaved Sparsity (FIS): alternating subsets of anchor latent frames across middle blocks while preserving dense computation in sensitive boundary blocks and final steps, keeping dense kernel compatibility.
5zceymhFF7.key_idea: Interleaves sparse subsets of latent frames across video DiT blocks while protecting sensitive blocks and steps to refresh all frames without custom kernels.
5zceymhFF7.evidence: Evaluated on Wan 2.2 and HunyuanVideo 1.5 (720p, down to 4 steps) using 100 prompts with VBench scores and component ablations.
5zceymhFF7.claimed_gains: Achieves 2.4x speedup on 720p Video DiTs (Wan 2.2 and HunyuanVideo 1.5) in as few as 4 steps without retraining.
5zceymhFF7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that targeting intra-step latent-frame sparsity is well-motivated for few-step video DiTs and cleanly compatible with standard dense kernels without retraining.
5zceymhFF7.main_concern: Reviewers cite weak quality-preservation evidence (aggregate VBench on only 100 prompts without motion-specific metrics), insufficient justification of the block-selection criterion, and missing implementation details.

U3m52t3ftc.one_liner: Improves TD-MPC sample efficiency via multi-horizon value averaging, a value-equivalent dynamics ensemble, and pessimistic reanalyze.
U3m52t3ftc.problem: Learned dynamics and value networks introduce compounding estimation errors in TD-MPC planners, hurting sample efficiency in continuous control.
U3m52t3ftc.method: EfficientTDMPC augments the BMPC/TD-MPC planner with three modifications: averaging value estimates across multiple rollout horizons, training a value-equivalent dynamics ensemble to average multi-head rollouts, and applying pessimistic reanalyze for early-terminating tasks.
U3m52t3ftc.key_idea: Reduces planner estimation error by averaging values across multiple horizons and a value-equivalent dynamics ensemble, paired with pessimistic reanalyze.
U3m52t3ftc.evidence: Evaluated on HumanoidBench and the DeepMind Control Suite against BMPC, TD-MPC variants, and other RL baselines with component ablations.
U3m52t3ftc.claimed_gains: Reaches BMPC's final aggregated performance on HumanoidBench and DeepMind Control Suite using 57% fewer environment steps.
U3m52t3ftc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the modifications are simple, intuitive, and empirically improve sample efficiency over strong TD-MPC/BMPC baselines.
U3m52t3ftc.main_concern: Reviewers point out limited theoretical or mechanistic analysis of why each change helps, and note that per-task gains in the appendix are concentrated on a small subset of HumanoidBench tasks.

aotmrz9sYS.one_liner: Jointly trains a latent tokenizer and flow-based dynamics predictor end-to-end on Vision Foundation Model features for future prediction.
aotmrz9sYS.problem: Forecasting on frozen Vision Foundation Model features or separately trained tokenizers leaves representations unoptimized for temporal predictability.
aotmrz9sYS.method: Latent-Foresight jointly optimizes a latent tokenizer and a flow-based generative dynamics model end-to-end in VFM feature space, incorporating stabilization designs to prevent latent collapse and align reconstruction with generative forecasting objectives across resolutions.
aotmrz9sYS.key_idea: Jointly optimizes a VFM-feature latent tokenizer and flow-based generative dynamics model end-to-end with anti-collapse alignment between reconstruction and prediction.
aotmrz9sYS.evidence: Evaluated against two-stage autoencoder baselines and direct frozen-VFM forecasting on future scene understanding tasks (including nuScenes and Cityscapes) across multiple horizons with ablations.
aotmrz9sYS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly optimizing tokenization and temporal prediction is well-motivated and shows consistent gains over two-stage baselines with informative anti-collapse ablations.
aotmrz9sYS.main_concern: Reviewers note limited conceptual novelty over prior joint video world models and Representation Autoencoders (RAE/VideoRAE), narrow autonomous-driving evaluation, and missing training-cost comparisons.

cEmuTAg4qE.one_liner: Characterizes category-dependent unlearning regret in combinatorial semi-bandits and constructs an Envelope learner enabling exact replay from retained feedback.
cEmuTAg4qE.problem: Withdrawing feedback in a sequential learner can alter its stopping decision and require observations that were never collected during the original run.
cEmuTAg4qE.method: The paper studies exact unlearning under protected action categories in combinatorial semi-bandits, proving matching regret lower and upper bounds up to log factors. Its gap-agnostic learner, Envelope, uses a completion-envelope missing-feedback rule ensuring erased runs stop no later than the original run for exact replay.
cEmuTAg4qE.key_idea: Uses a completion-envelope missing-feedback rule so erased semi-bandit executions stop no later than factual runs, guaranteeing exact replay from already-collected feedback.
cEmuTAg4qE.evidence: Proves matching regret bounds for covered product actions with unique optima and comparable gaps, supported by experiments on learning cost, feedback collection, and replay.
cEmuTAg4qE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the interesting problem formulation, matching category-dependent regret characterization, and constructive exact-replay guarantee.
cEmuTAg4qE.main_concern: Reviewers find the notation-heavy main text not self-contained (relying heavily on appendices) and note that the single-interaction deletion model needs clearer operational motivation.

8RnvRHTaXF.one_liner: Performs buffer-free differentially private continual learning via nearest-prototype classification in a frozen-backbone embedding space with DP-friendly preservation losses.
8RnvRHTaXF.problem: Continual learning under differential privacy struggles to balance forgetting prevention, strict privacy without stored buffers, and decision interpretability.
8RnvRHTaXF.method: Built on frozen pretrained backbones, the framework adapts a linear projection and represents each class with a single DP prototype for nearest-prototype classification, using DP-friendly representation-preservation losses and synthetic support. Prototypes are interpreted via nearest public pretraining images or generated synthetic samples.
8RnvRHTaXF.key_idea: Maintains one differentially private class prototype per class under a frozen backbone with DP-friendly preservation losses for buffer-free, interpretable nearest-prototype continual learning.
8RnvRHTaXF.evidence: Includes theoretical analysis of Gaussian prototype perturbations and experiments on Split-CIFAR-100 and Split-ImageNet-R against interpretable and non-interpretable DP continual learning baselines.
8RnvRHTaXF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the strict buffer-free privacy awareness, appropriate baseline choice, and practical DP prototype continual learning formulation.
8RnvRHTaXF.main_concern: Reviewers criticize freezing the backbone (limiting plasticity on ImageNet-R), un-retuned loss ablations, pretraining overlap in public-proxy interpretation, and theory ignoring projection drift.

STbKHlEcyS.one_liner: Trains mobile GUI agents via RL using a pretrained world model for simulated rollouts and in-thought action consequence previewing.
STbKHlEcyS.problem: Training mobile GUI agents with online RL requires costly, unstable, and slow interactions with live Android environments.
STbKHlEcyS.method: WM-R1 replaces real Android environments with a pretrained world model to generate massively parallelized, step-level rollouts during RL training, while embedding world-model previews into the agent's reasoning process. It optimizes a multi-dimensional rule-based reward covering task success, efficiency, and world-model use on 2,000 curated tasks.
STbKHlEcyS.key_idea: Uses a pretrained world model both as the rollout simulator during GRPO training and as an embedded action-preview tool inside the GUI agent's reasoning loop.
STbKHlEcyS.evidence: Evaluated on Android mobile navigation and grounding benchmarks across Qwen2.5-VL (3B and 7B) against GRPO-only and inference-time simulation baselines.
STbKHlEcyS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that replacing costly live Android interactions with world-model rollouts and action previews is a practical, clear approach with consistent gains across model scales.
STbKHlEcyS.main_concern: Reviewers note that the main baseline (UI-R1) is offline rather than live-environment RL, world-model rollout fidelity is unmeasured, and ablations fail to isolate simulated training from test-time world-model use.

s2TfhwVlAZ.one_liner: Fast-VLA runs a frozen 4B VLM once per episode to cache multi-layer KV task memory queried by a lightweight online actor.
s2TfhwVlAZ.problem: Vision-language-action policies repeatedly run multi-billion-parameter backbones for every action chunk even though high-level task understanding changes much more slowly than robot state.
s2TfhwVlAZ.method: Fast-VLA invokes a frozen 4B VLM once per episode on the instruction and initial views to build a fixed multi-layer key-value task memory. During execution, a lightweight multi-view actor fuses learned time- and arm-indexed queries with current visual and proprioceptive observations to retrieve from this memory and output action chunks.
s2TfhwVlAZ.key_idea: Caches a frozen VLM's multi-layer KV states once per episode and queries them online with a lightweight actor conditioned on current visual-proprioceptive state.
s2TfhwVlAZ.evidence: Evaluated in simulation on RoboTwin 2.0 (Clean and Randomized), LIBERO, and LIBERO-Plus on an A100 GPU, plus task-memory swap ablations.
s2TfhwVlAZ.claimed_gains: Achieves 92.46% and 92.40% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean and Randomized, 95.95% and 79.11% on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus, 10.9-17.1x amortized inference speedup over three baselines, and 1.22 GiB post-prefill online resident memory.
s2TfhwVlAZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating slow episode-level VLM conditioning from fast closed-loop control is well-motivated and yields large inference speedups in simulation.
s2TfhwVlAZ.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about fixed episode-level memory failing under scene changes or unexpected interactions, lack of real-world robot validation, and non-apples-to-apples efficiency comparisons against CoT and world-model VLAs.

9BRT7SVELI.one_liner: WoRL post-trains autoregressive video world models with Parallel Clean-Prefix Attention, a history-conditioned Next-Video Reward Model, and revisit-centered rollouts.
9BRT7SVELI.problem: Scaling RL post-training for autoregressive video world models is hindered by train-test mismatch over long contexts, lack of history-aware rewards, and rare exposure to accumulated consistency errors.
9BRT7SVELI.method: WoRL combines (1) Parallel Clean-Prefix Attention, context-aware scheduling, and distributed execution to eliminate intra-clip train-test mismatch in DiffusionNFT; (2) a Next-Video Reward Model (NVRM) trained on 312.4k graph-constructed preference pairs without human annotation to score clips conditioned on history; and (3) revisit-centered trajectories that revisit observed scenes to expose drift.
9BRT7SVELI.key_idea: Scales full-attention video world-model RL by pairing Parallel Clean-Prefix Attention with an annotation-free history-conditioned reward model and scene-revisiting rollouts.
9BRT7SVELI.evidence: Evaluated with quantitative/qualitative video world-model benchmarks, update-latency measurements, and a small human evaluation of consistency and physical plausibility.
9BRT7SVELI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that long-horizon consistency in video world models is an important target and appreciate the synergy of PCPA efficiency and history-conditioned annotation-free reward modeling.
9BRT7SVELI.main_concern: Reviewers note insufficient human evaluation sample size and protocol details for NVRM, unclear attribution of gains across individual components versus data/budget, and missing ablations over chunk count J.
